capability: Customer onboarding and CIP (customer identification program)
business_problem: Know who controls an account before it transacts.
why_industry_requires: Banks are BSA financial institutions with a mandated CIP.
daf_equivalent_explanation: A 501(c)(3) sponsor paying its own grants is not a BSA financial institution (OB-32); it needs identity proofing for fraud/authorization and sanctions screening, not a CIP. A CIP applies only by contract (custodian/processor) or if a vendor holding funds is an MSB.
complexity_challenge: Do not import bank CIP document-collection workflows; collect only what the applicability register says is required and what fraud risk justifies.
automation_rationale: Identity proofing via partner; deterministic applicability resolution.
automation_risks: Over-collection of PII; labelling sponsor checks 'KYC required' without basis.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel sign-off on OB-32; contract review of custodian/processor CIP flow-downs.
analogy_breaks_down: Bank CIP is a legal duty to the regulator; DAF identity proofing protects the sponsor's exclusive legal control and prevents account takeover.
evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/31/1010.230 (accessed 2026-11-23) [primary, read: (e)(3)(ii) nonprofit control-prong only; (f) covered FI per 1010.605(e)(1)]

capability: Beneficial ownership / CDD on legal-entity customers
business_problem: Identify natural persons behind entities.
why_industry_requires: 31 CFR 1010.230 binds covered financial institutions (banks, broker-dealers, mutual funds).
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor is itself the legal-entity customer of its banks/custodians; as a nonprofit it is subject only to the control prong (1010.230(e)(3)(ii)). FinCEN FIN-2026-R001 removed re-verification at each new account. For donors that are entities (corporate/foundation contributors) the sponsor has no CDD duty; related-party and §4958/§4943 screens need ownership facts for other reasons.
complexity_challenge: Keep one 'controlling persons / authorized signers' register for each sponsor legal entity, exportable to banks at account opening; do not run CDD on donors.
automation_rationale: Signer/control-person register is master data with versioned evidence.
automation_risks: Stale signer lists at banks letting departed officers act (see TVF-123).
validation_evidence_needed: Bank account-opening packet requirements for each sponsor bank.
analogy_breaks_down: CDD exists to detect hidden owners laundering through accounts; DAF ownership facts serve excess-benefit and business-holdings tests, not AML.
evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/31/1010.230 (accessed 2026-11-23) [primary, read: (e)(3)(ii) nonprofit control-prong only; (f) covered FI per 1010.605(e)(1)]

https://fincen.gov/resources/statutes-and-regulations/cdd-final-rule (accessed 2026-11-23) [read: lists FIN-2026-R001 exceptive relief order]; https://www.dlapiper.com/en-lu/insights/publications/2026/03/fincen-issues-exceptive-relief-from-cdd-rule-requirements (accessed 2026-11-23) [search-result summary]

capability: Account hierarchies and relationships
business_problem: Represent households, entities, sub-accounts, signers.
why_industry_requires: Banks model customer/relationship/account hierarchies for exposure and entitlements.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor > program > fund > participants; pooled vs segregated custody; multi-fund custody attribution.
complexity_challenge: Existing design is adequate; no bank-style relationship pricing hierarchy needed.
automation_risks: Ancestor capacity checks missed (covered by FIN-009).
analogy_breaks_down: Bank hierarchies aggregate credit exposure; DAF hierarchies aggregate legal control and grant capacity.

capability: Money movement orchestration across rails (outbound grants)
business_problem: Move money once, to the right party, with proof.
why_industry_requires: Core bank/payment-hub function.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant disbursement is the DAF's dominant outbound flow.
complexity_challenge: Seven orthogonal dimensions are correct internally but the payment class (grant vs fee vs investment vs refund) and rail eligibility matrix is not stated; add the matrix rather than more states.
automation_rationale: State transitions are rule-driven; AI only summarizes exceptions.
automation_risks: Blind retry after timeout; premature settlement posting.
validation_evidence_needed: Provider contract evidence of idempotency and status query (TVR-PAY-002).
analogy_breaks_down: Banks own the ledger of record for the account; a DAF sponsor is a bank customer and only sees its side.

capability: ACH origination (credits for grants, debits for contributions)
business_problem: Originate ACH within network rules.
why_industry_requires: Nacha Operating Rules bind Originators via the ODFI agreement.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor (or its administrator as Third-Party Sender) is a non-consumer Originator of CCD credits to charities and of PPD/WEB debits from donors.
complexity_challenge: Existing text treats Nacha as '[S] contractual' with no concrete Originator obligations; needs a rail obligation register (UNB-XIN-BNK-001) and the specific WEB/fraud-monitoring/return-rate controls.
automation_rationale: Validation, return-rate counters and reinitiation rules are deterministic.
automation_risks: Treating Nacha as optional; misclassifying R10 vs R29 windows.
validation_evidence_needed: ODFI agreement; who is Originator of record (sponsor vs administrator).
analogy_breaks_down: Network-rule duties are contractual, not statutory, but enforceable by ODFI fines/termination.

capability: ACH Notification of Change (NOC) handling
business_problem: Apply corrected account data from RDFIs.
why_industry_requires: Nacha requires Originators to act on NOCs within set times.
daf_equivalent_explanation: NOC changes a pinned, verified destination and conflicts with destination-change controls.
complexity_challenge: Treat NOC as an evidence-bearing proposed destination change routed through the same destination-evidence table (GRT-017), auto-approvable only when account owner unchanged.
automation_rationale: Deterministic auto-apply for format-only corrections; human for owner/routing change.
automation_risks: Fraud via NOC spoofing is low but routing changes still redirect funds.
validation_evidence_needed: NOC timing obligation text from Nacha rules (not read).
analogy_breaks_down: None material.

capability: Wire transfers and recall
business_problem: High-value same-day credit transfers.
why_industry_requires: Banks execute wires under UCC Article 4A.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Large grants, sponsor-to-sponsor transfers, international grants.
complexity_challenge: Model recall strictly as a request: under UCC 4A-211 cancellation after acceptance needs the receiving bank's agreement and, at the beneficiary bank, only for unauthorized/duplicate/mistaken orders. No platform 'cancel wire' affordance.
automation_rationale: Release of a wire is irreversible; independent confirmation is the control.
automation_risks: AI-drafted confirmation emails being used as 'independent' channel.
analogy_breaks_down: Banks can debit/credit their own customers; the sponsor can only ask.
evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/ucc/4A/4A-211 (accessed 2026-11-23) [primary, read: cancellation after acceptance only with receiving-bank agreement; beneficiary bank limited to unauthorized/duplicate/mistake]

capability: Instant payments (RTP / FedNow)
business_problem: Irrevocable real-time credit push.
why_industry_requires: Faster settlement; $10m network limit (FedNow from 2025-11-12; RTP).
daf_equivalent_explanation: Possible for urgent disaster grants; irrevocable, no return right, and charities' banks may not receive. No existing requirement addresses instant rails.
complexity_challenge: Do not add a new rail until demand is proven; cover it via the rail-eligibility matrix with default Ineligible for grants.
automation_risks: Instant + irrevocable + BEC = fastest loss path.
validation_evidence_needed: Sponsor bank support; receiving-bank reach for charities.
analogy_breaks_down: Consumer instant payments assume payer knows payee; DAF payees are vetted organizations where speed rarely matters.
evidence: https://www.frbservices.org/news/communications/111225-fednow-transaction-limit-increase (accessed 2026-11-23) [search-result summary: FedNow network limit $10m from 2025-11-12; RTP $10m]

capability: Check issuance, positive pay and payee-name positive pay
business_problem: Prevent altered/counterfeit/stolen check payment.
why_industry_requires: Banks offer positive pay; FinCEN flagged mail-theft check fraud (FIN-2023-Alert003).
daf_equivalent_explanation: Many DAF sponsors still pay by check; Treasury reports checks 16x more likely lost/stolen/altered than EFT.
complexity_challenge: Issue file must be acknowledged before print release; payee-name match where offered; default exception decision = return.
automation_rationale: File generation and exception default are deterministic; pay decisions on exceptions are human.
automation_risks: Exception decisions defaulting to 'pay' at cut-off.
validation_evidence_needed: Bank positive-pay file spec and exception log export (EXT-03).
analogy_breaks_down: Banks see the presented item; sponsor sees only its issue file—the control works only if issue file is complete and timely.

capability: Check stop-payment, void, stale-dating and reissue
business_problem: Recover from lost/uncashed checks.
why_industry_requires: Standard treasury operations.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Covered by GRT-005 lifecycle and PAY-04 fixture.
complexity_challenge: Adequate; ensure stop/void evidence comes from bank positive-pay acknowledgment, not internal flag.
analogy_breaks_down: None.

capability: Unclaimed property / escheat of uncashed grant checks
business_problem: Report and remit dormant owed property.
why_industry_requires: State unclaimed property acts bind holders; business-to-business exemptions vary (e.g., VA has one; NY does not).
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor is holder; charity payee is owner. Whether a voided DAF grant check is owed property is unsettled (REG-045). Fund balances are not escheatable absent counsel record (RR-UNB-WF-015-r1).
complexity_challenge: Prevent the problem upstream: ACH-default for grantees plus outreach before stale-dating eliminates most escheat volume; keep a counsel-maintained per-state rule table for the residue.
automation_rationale: Aging and report-file generation deterministic; state applicability is counsel-owned configuration.
automation_risks: Applying a single dormancy period nationally; silently re-crediting funds.
validation_evidence_needed: Per-state statute review for charitable payees; priority-rule application.
analogy_breaks_down: Bank escheat concerns customer deposits; DAF escheat concerns outbound instruments to organizations, where charities can be located easily.
evidence: https://www.vscpa.com/article/found-money-maybe-not and https://www.osc.ny.gov/files/unclaimed-funds/reporters/pdf/handbook.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23) [search-result summaries only: VA business-to-business exemption for outstanding checks; NY no B2B exemption] - low confidence

capability: Bank reconciliation and statement ingestion
business_problem: Prove ledger cash equals bank cash daily.
why_industry_requires: Core control in every bank customer's treasury.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Required for grant payable, clearing and contribution receipts.
complexity_challenge: Reconciliation exists as a concept but there is no rule that every bank debit must match an authorized platform instruction (detects out-of-band portal payments).
automation_rationale: Matching on amount/date/reference is deterministic; AI only proposes matches for residue.
validation_evidence_needed: Bank statement format availability (BAI2/camt.053) per bank — not verified.
analogy_breaks_down: None.

capability: Out-of-band payment prevention (bank portal entitlements, ACH debit block)
business_problem: Stop payments that bypass the platform.
why_industry_requires: Banks offer entitlements, dual control, ACH debit blocks/filters.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Platform controls are void if staff can key payments in the bank portal (TVR-PAY-004, TVF-223).
complexity_challenge: Make the bank portal read-only for platform-originated rails; detect rather than trust: daily unmatched-debit check.
automation_risks: False incidents from bank fees; mitigated by fee-type whitelist.
analogy_breaks_down: None.

capability: Dual control and payment limits
business_problem: No single person can move money; size-based authority.
why_industry_requires: Bank treasury standard.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Covered by sponsor authority matrix and SoD rules.
complexity_challenge: Do not add a second limit system in the bank; align bank-side limits to platform authority matrix by attestation.
automation_risks: Agents filling SoD pairs (covered by rev3 B21).
analogy_breaks_down: None.

capability: Payment fraud monitoring (BEC, payee impersonation, account takeover)
business_problem: Detect payments induced by false pretenses.
why_industry_requires: Nacha 2026 rules require non-consumer Originators to run risk-based processes to identify entries authorized under False Pretenses (Phase 2 eff. 2026-06-19/22).
daf_equivalent_explanation: Disclosed sponsor losses are payment redirection/BEC (Prosperity $500,845 net; TNC $524,983; WashU $565,787 ACH redirection; Givinga $316,184).
complexity_challenge: Most of the control already exists as destination evidence; what's missing is the Nacha-required documented risk-based program, its annual review record and credit-origination monitoring rules.
automation_rationale: Deterministic rules for destination change, first-payment, velocity; AI may rank alerts but not clear them.
analogy_breaks_down: Banks monitor across many customers; sponsor sees only its own payees—network-level signals must come from bank/provider.

capability: Suspicious activity escalation (SAR)
business_problem: Report suspicious transactions to FinCEN.
why_industry_requires: BSA mandate for financial institutions.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor is not a BSA FI (OB-32); no SAR filing duty. Practice: escalate suspected fraud/diversion to counsel, the bank, law enforcement; OFAC blocking/reporting IS binding (OB-30).
complexity_challenge: Do not build a SAR module; build a 'refer to bank/law enforcement' case outcome.
automation_risks: Mislabeling referrals as SARs; tipping-off concepts do not apply but confidentiality still prudent.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel confirmation of OB-32 for each operating model (administrator holding funds may be MSB).
analogy_breaks_down: SAR regime protects the financial system from customers; sponsor is the customer.

capability: Account restrictions and holds
business_problem: Freeze activity on risk events.
why_industry_requires: Banks place holds/restraints.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Global holds, fund holds, recipient holds, Blocked property.
complexity_challenge: Adequate.
analogy_breaks_down: None.

capability: Cash forecasting and disbursement-account liquidity
business_problem: Have cash in the right account at settlement time.
why_industry_requires: Treasury function; ACH credit files debit the Originator at settlement; checks clear unpredictably.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Per-grant funding states exist (FIN-008) but no account-level daily cash position combining scheduled releases, outstanding checks, T+1 liquidation proceeds and provisional contributions.
complexity_challenge: A deterministic projection from existing facts, not a forecasting model.
automation_rationale: Projection from scheduled events; no ML needed.
automation_risks: Using expected check clearing as certain.
validation_evidence_needed: Custodian sweep timing; bank prefunding rules.
analogy_breaks_down: Bank ALM forecasts deposit behaviour; DAF disbursement cash is almost fully scheduled.

capability: Deposit concentration and FDIC exposure
business_problem: Limit uninsured exposure to one bank.
why_industry_requires: Treasury policy.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Large DAF cash in operating/disbursement accounts above FDIC limits; sponsor investment policy usually governs.
complexity_challenge: Sponsor treasury policy parameter + report; not a platform workflow.
analogy_breaks_down: None.
evidence: unverified — general industry knowledge (FDIC standard maximum deposit insurance $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category)

capability: Financial statement generation
business_problem: Produce GAAP statements.
why_industry_requires: Banks produce customer statements and own GAAP statements.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Fund statements and sponsor books.
complexity_challenge: Out of payment scope.

capability: Banking partner integration (files, APIs, statements)
business_problem: Exchange instructions and evidence with banks.
why_industry_requires: Core integration.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Deferred by PAY-DEF-001; adapter contracts and simulated adapter required (UNB-PAY-007).
complexity_challenge: Keep one adapter contract; file-based (ACH/positive pay) and API-based providers behind it.

capability: Business continuity for payments
business_problem: Pay safely during outages.
why_industry_requires: Bank/regulatory resilience expectations.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Outage intake queued not approved; reconcile provider status before resuming.
complexity_challenge: Manual fallback runs through the gate; no emergency bank-portal payments.

capability: Customer communication for payments (remittance)
business_problem: Payee can identify and apply funds.
why_industry_requires: Remittance advice/addenda.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Charities struggle to identify DAF grants; Ren/Chariot shared enrollment networks emerged.
complexity_challenge: Use CCD+ addenda/remittance with grant ID; publish to recipient portal; no separate remittance system.
automation_risks: Leaking donor identity contrary to anonymity choice.

capability: Payment lifecycle and status projection
business_problem: Show truthful status.
why_industry_requires: Payment processors expose lifecycle.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Covered by REQ-X-083 dimensions and UNB-PAY-009 UI.
complexity_challenge: Adequate.

capability: Card contributions acceptance
business_problem: Accept donor card gifts.
why_industry_requires: Merchant acquiring; PCI DSS via acquirer contract.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Some sponsors (PayPal CGF, Blackbaud GF) carry material card fees; card acceptance is optional by model. No requirement defines card dispute handling.
complexity_challenge: Use hosted fields/tokenization to stay in reduced PCI scope; never store PAN.
analogy_breaks_down: Retail merchants deliver goods; a charity 'merchant' delivers nothing, so 'not as described' disputes rarely fit but 'fraud' and 'not recognized' do.
evidence: unverified — general industry knowledge (PCI DSS scope reduction via hosted fields/tokenization)

capability: Disputes and chargebacks (card contributions)
business_problem: Handle involuntary reversals.
why_industry_requires: Card network rules; cardholder dispute windows generally 120 days, some up to 540.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Not covered. Collides with irrevocable-acceptance rule (UNB-RCN-FIN-013) and acknowledgment issuance.
complexity_challenge: Default to accept-and-reverse for small amounts; human decision to contest only above threshold.
automation_risks: Contesting donor disputes harms trust; not contesting invites friendly fraud.
validation_evidence_needed: Acquirer dispute API; network reason code list.
analogy_breaks_down: Retail representment argues delivery; sponsor argues authorization evidence only.
evidence: https://usa.visa.com/dam/VCOM/global/support-legal/documents/faq-apr-disputes.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23) [search-result summary: 120 days, some reasons up to 540 days]

capability: Refunds
business_problem: Return money voluntarily.
why_industry_requires: Merchants refund customers.
daf_equivalent_explanation: After acceptance value leaves only via grant (UNB-RCN-FIN-013); pre-acceptance return of property never accepted is permitted with counsel exception. Duplicate charges are the main legitimate refund case.
complexity_challenge: Name it 'ReturnOfUnacceptedProperty', not refund; only before acceptance.
automation_risks: Refund used to launder (card in, refund to other instrument).
analogy_breaks_down: Retail refunds are customer service; DAF refunds after acceptance would be a taxable distribution risk.

capability: Failed payments and retries (contributions)
business_problem: Collect recurring debits.
why_industry_requires: Billing dunning; Nacha reinitiation limits.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Recurring contributions exist; retry rules absent. Nacha: reinitiated entries must keep same amount and 'RETRY PYMT'; unauthorized returns may not be reinitiated.
complexity_challenge: Prefer no automatic retry for DAF contributions except R01/R09 once; donor-initiated retry otherwise.
validation_evidence_needed: Nacha rules text on reinitiation limits (not fully verified).
analogy_breaks_down: Subscriptions owe money; DAF donors owe nothing—dunning is inappropriate.

capability: Scheduled and recurring payments
business_problem: Execute schedules idempotently.
why_industry_requires: Billing/payments core.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Recurring grants (GRT-004) and recurring contributions; Reg E 1005.10(b) binds any payee obtaining preauthorized debits from consumer accounts.
complexity_challenge: Recurring grant side covered; recurring contribution authorization evidence (Reg E) missing.

capability: Transaction fees and manual processing charges
business_problem: Price and recover rail costs.
why_industry_requires: Processors charge per-transaction; merchants pass through.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Card fees ~0.30% of grants at Blackbaud GF; PayPal CGF transaction costs 1.58%; Benevity manual check fee higher of $35 or 8%. Fee charging to funds covered by FeeBase (FIN-005) and AUA-05; donor-covers-fee gross/net treatment missing.
complexity_challenge: Record actual processor fee per transaction once; derive both fee charges and cost-to-serve from it.

capability: Idempotency and duplicate detection
business_problem: Exactly-once financial effect.
why_industry_requires: Payment API standard.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Covered.
complexity_challenge: Add intake-side duplicate gift detection (same donor, amount, instrument within window) – currently only provider-event dedup.

capability: Card-testing / enumeration attack defense
business_problem: Stop fraudsters using donation forms to test stolen cards.
why_industry_requires: Merchants with low-friction forms are targeted.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Embedded/public donation forms (REQ-X-063) are classic targets; DAF contribution forms with low minimums equally.
complexity_challenge: Velocity limits + bot friction + minimum amount; deterministic first.
automation_rationale: Rule thresholds work well; ML optional via acquirer.
evidence: unverified — general industry knowledge (PCI DSS scope reduction via hosted fields/tokenization)

capability: Processor reconciliation (gross, fee, net, payout)
business_problem: Tie processor payouts to gifts.
why_industry_requires: Merchant reconciliation.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Processor settles net of fees in batches; must match to individual gross gifts.
complexity_challenge: Three-way: gift gross ↔ processor transaction ↔ payout batch ↔ bank credit.

capability: Securities contributions via DTC free delivery
business_problem: Receive donor shares.
why_industry_requires: DTC book-entry delivery between participants.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Main noncash gift path; deliveries often arrive without donor identity; FINRA ACATS (Rule 11870) is for same-customer account transfers (title mismatch is an exception ground), so gifts use non-ACATS DTC delivery.
complexity_challenge: Require intent pre-notification with CUSIP/quantity/delivering participant and deterministic match; suspense otherwise.
analogy_breaks_down: Broker transfers keep owner; gift changes owner—ACATS framing misleads UI copy.
evidence: https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/rulebooks/finra-rules/11870 (accessed 2026-11-23) [primary, read: ACATS customer account transfer; title-mismatch exception; 1+3 business days]

capability: Liquidation-to-cash timing (T+1)
business_problem: Convert securities to grantable cash.
why_industry_requires: SEC T+1 since 2024-05-28.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Affects completed-gift vs proceeds dates and grant funding timing.
complexity_challenge: Use rail calendar for projected proceeds.

capability: Custodian cash sweep and movement authorization
business_problem: Every custodial movement authorized.
why_industry_requires: Custody controls.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Rev3 B19 daily matching of custodian movements.

capability: Payment cost-to-serve attribution
business_problem: Know cost per transaction per rail and per exception.
why_industry_requires: Banks/processors price by rail and exception.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Operational metrics mention cost per resolved case; no per-rail cost driver emission.
complexity_challenge: Emit cost-driver facts from payment events; let economics model price them.

capability: AUM definition registry (fee base, Schedule D value, serviced AUM, advisor RAUM support, performance base)
business_problem: One 'AUM' number is reused for fees, filings, partner economics and marketing although each needs a different inclusion rule.
why_industry_requires: Wealth managers keep regulatory AUM, billable AUM and firm AUM distinct because each drives a different obligation.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor needs fee base, Schedule D line 4 value, partner-economics AUM and performance base; DAF assets are sponsor-owned, so 'client AUM' language is misleading.
complexity_challenge: Do not build an AUM engine; one named-definition registry over the ledger/valuation snapshots is enough.
automation_rationale: Each definition is a filter + valuation-version over authoritative snapshots.
automation_risks: A mislabeled figure on a partner invoice or 990.
validation_evidence_needed: CPA/CFO sign-off of each definition; fixture with pending contributions, accrued fees, NAV-embedded fees.
analogy_breaks_down: Advisor RAUM is a SEC Form ADV concept for the adviser; the sponsor has no RAUM.

capability: Investment book of record (positions, lots, trade-date activity, pending settlements)
business_problem: Capacity, rebalancing and statements need intraday positions before the custodian's end-of-day statement.
why_industry_requires: Asset managers run an IBOR separate from the accounting book (ABOR) to trade on current positions.
daf_equivalent_explanation: DAF platform needs trade-date positions for liquidity/capacity and settled positions for cash; the custodian remains the external position record.
complexity_challenge: Do not build a separate IBOR store; trade-date and settlement-date are two views over one investment subledger.
automation_rationale: Positions are arithmetic over normalized custody events.
validation_evidence_needed: Reconciliation of trade-date view to custodian at T+1.
analogy_breaks_down: Sponsors rarely trade intraday; IBOR freshness needs are far lower than an asset manager's.

industry: Outsourced fund administration and transfer agency
capability: Book-of-record designation per entity and function (ABOR, IBOR, unit register, fund statements)
business_problem: Sponsors that outsource fund accounting to an administrator or OCIO have two sets of books; nobody states which one the auditor relies on.
why_industry_requires: Fund administration contracts name the book of record and the shadow; disputes are resolved against the designated record.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Unbound may be ABOR for fund attribution but a shadow of an administrator's GL, or vice versa.
complexity_challenge: Make designation a configuration fact with three values per function (authoritative / shadow / not-used), not separate code paths.
automation_rationale: Designation is a sponsor contract fact.
automation_risks: Wrong designation lets a shadow feed overwrite authoritative books.
validation_evidence_needed: Sponsor contract review; dual-run fixture with deliberate administrator error.
analogy_breaks_down: Fund administrators service legally separate funds with external investors; DAF 'funds' are internal designations of one charity.

capability: Investment policy statement and committee governance (prudence basis)
business_problem: Sponsors must evidence prudent investment decisions; §4944 does not apply to DAFs, so the governing standard is state prudent-investor/UPMIFA-type law.
why_industry_requires: Institutional investors document IPS, committee minutes and manager reviews to evidence prudence.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor investment committee approves menus, managers and rebalancing parameters.
complexity_challenge: Store IPS versions and committee decisions as evidence linked to pool/mandate configs; do not encode prudence as rules.
automation_risks: AI-drafted IPS adopted without committee deliberation.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel confirmation of applicable state law (UPMIFA applicability to DAF assets unverified).
analogy_breaks_down: Wealth-manager suitability is client-centric; here the 'client' is the charity, not the donor.

capability: Model portfolios and pool menus
business_problem: Donors/advisors choose among sponsor-approved strategies.
why_industry_requires: Wealth platforms distribute models to many accounts.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor-approved pool menu or advisor models within sponsor policy.
complexity_challenge: Most sponsors need only a pool menu; model-to-SMA trade generation should stay with the advisor/custodian.
analogy_breaks_down: Donor 'allocation' moves internal units, not securities, in a unitized program.

capability: Rebalancing (pool-level and advisor SMA drift)
business_problem: Allocations drift; sponsor policy sets bands.
why_industry_requires: Asset managers rebalance to targets with pre-trade checks.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Pool rebalancing is the OCIO/manager's job; the platform needs drift monitoring and fund-level re-election, not trade generation.
complexity_challenge: Over-scoped if Unbound generates trades for pools run by external managers; restrict to monitoring + approved instructions.
automation_risks: AI-proposed rebalance treated as advice (see RR-UNB-INV-019-r1).
analogy_breaks_down: No tax-loss harvesting motive for a tax-exempt holder.

capability: Investment restrictions and pre/post-trade compliance (prohibited, concentration, §4943 holdings)
business_problem: Sponsor must stop prohibited holdings and monitor excess business holdings.
why_industry_requires: Investment compliance engines enforce restricted lists pre-trade.
daf_equivalent_explanation: §4943(e) applies to DAFs; donor-gifted concentrated stock is common.
complexity_challenge: Pre-trade checks only where Unbound originates orders; otherwise post-trade monitoring on custody feed.
analogy_breaks_down: Restrictions also bind gifts in (acceptance), not only trades.

capability: Advisor-managed DAF accounts (SMA per fund) with sponsor as client of record
business_problem: Advisors want to keep managing assets their clients give; the sponsor, not the donor, is the advisory client.
why_industry_requires: In wealth management the account owner signs the advisory agreement and receives Form ADV disclosures.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor must contract with the advisor, approve the mandate and control fee debits; existing requirements cover discretion and §4958 screen but not the advisory-agreement/client-of-record facts.
complexity_challenge: Keep one 'mandate' object: agreement version, client=sponsor, fee schedule, account scope, revocation.
automation_rationale: Contract facts plus deterministic fee checks.
automation_risks: Donor treated as client; advisor bills donor-related fees.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel on Advisers Act client status; sample advisor agreements.
analogy_breaks_down: A wealth client can fire the advisor; here only the sponsor can, though donors recommend.
evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/80b-3 (accessed 2026-11-23): Advisers Act §203(b)(4) registration exemption limited to a charitable organization or its trustee/director/officer/employee/volunteer advising only charitable organizations, §3(c)(10)(B) funds or charitable trusts

capability: Advisor fee debit verification (custodian-debited fees from DAF accounts)
business_problem: Advisors usually send a billing file to the custodian, which debits the DAF account; the sponsor must authorize and verify each debit.
why_industry_requires: RIAs bill via custodian fee-debit with client authorization; custodians do not verify fee correctness.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor is the payer from charitable assets; an over-billed fee is an improper use of charitable assets and possibly a §4958 issue.
complexity_challenge: Deterministic recomputation from mandate fee schedule + valuation snapshot; tolerance-based exception.
automation_risks: Advisor uses a different valuation date; false breaks.
validation_evidence_needed: Sample custodian fee-debit files; advisor billing conventions (advance vs arrears).
analogy_breaks_down: Donor never pays the fee personally; fund pays.

capability: Custodian relationships and capability profiles
business_problem: Each custodian offers different feeds/entitlements.
why_industry_requires: Wealth platforms maintain custodian integration matrices.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Same.
complexity_challenge: Adequate.
analogy_breaks_down: None material.

capability: Mandatory corporate actions (splits, mergers, spin-offs)
business_problem: Positions and lots change without a trade.
why_industry_requires: Portfolio accounting processes CA feeds.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Same, plus effect on unit NAV.
complexity_challenge: Rely on custodian CA processing; reconcile, do not re-derive.
analogy_breaks_down: Cost-basis allocation matters only for 8282/UBTI cases.

capability: Voluntary corporate actions and proxy voting
business_problem: Elections (tenders, rights, dividend options) and shareholder votes need an authorized decision by a deadline.
why_industry_requires: Asset managers hold voting authority and a proxy-voting policy.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor holds legal title and votes; donors (especially of gifted company stock) often want to direct votes or tender decisions, which would be a donor control signal.
complexity_challenge: Default: delegate to pool manager/OCIO by policy; only SMA/gifted-stock positions need a sponsor election workflow.
automation_rationale: Deadlines and defaults deterministic; elections are human/manager decisions.
automation_risks: Missed election deadline; donor directing votes.
validation_evidence_needed: Custodian CA election channels; sponsor proxy policy.
analogy_breaks_down: Proxy voting for mutual-fund pools is done by the fund, not the sponsor.

capability: Trailing income and litigation recoveries (class actions) attribution
business_problem: Recoveries arrive years later for positions held in prior periods, sometimes by closed funds.
why_industry_requires: Asset managers file class-action claims and allocate proceeds to historical holders.
daf_equivalent_explanation: FI-35/OD-11 define destination after closure but not attribution among funds by holding period.
complexity_challenge: For unitized pools, credit the pool (current unitholders) by policy; per-fund historical attribution only for SMA/lot-owned positions.
automation_risks: Paying a closed fund's share to the wrong successor.
analogy_breaks_down: Mutual funds credit NAV on receipt; same convention fits pools.

capability: Performance reporting and benchmarking
business_problem: Donors/advisors/committees ask how strategies performed.
why_industry_requires: GIPS-style TWR reporting is a wealth/asset-manager norm.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Committee needs manager/pool TWR vs benchmark; a donor's fund needs simple change-in-value attribution. Fund-level MWR adds cost with little value.
complexity_challenge: Simplify: pool-level TWR from NAV series; fund statements show contributions/grants/fees/investment change only.
analogy_breaks_down: GIPS compliance is a marketing claim for asset managers; sponsors need not claim it.

capability: Sponsor/manager/advisor fee calculation
business_problem: Layered fees must not double-charge and must reconcile.
why_industry_requires: Wealth billing engines compute tiered bps fees.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor admin fee tiers 60/30/20/15 bps typical; advisor fees 0-2%.
complexity_challenge: Adequate after FeeBase contract.
analogy_breaks_down: Internal fee is not revenue on consolidated books.

capability: Cash sweep and uninvested cash management
business_problem: Cash awaiting investment or grant payment earns sweep yield and may exceed deposit insurance.
why_industry_requires: Wealth platforms disclose sweep programs and their economics.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sweep income attribution (fund, pool or sponsor) and FDIC concentration are unowned; affiliated-sponsor sweep economics are a conflict.
complexity_challenge: One declared sweep vehicle per cash account + one attribution rule; no per-fund sweep.
automation_risks: Sweep income silently retained by sponsor.
analogy_breaks_down: Donor has no deposit; insurance is per depositor (sponsor).
evidence: https://coloradogivesfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Colorado-Gives-Foundation-December-31-2025-Audited-Financial-Statement-Final.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23): Note 2 'Donor-advised funds are net assets where the Foundation has been granted variance power'; 'Unconditional grants are recorded as expenses and liabilities when they are approved'; agency endowments/designations accounted for as liabilities; alternative investments recorded with a 1-3 month statement lag; NAV practical expedient investments excluded from hierarchy; Note 3 liquidity table; UBI tax recognized when return filed

capability: Alternative and illiquid holdings (private stock, real estate, LP interests) valuation and lagged NAV
business_problem: GP statements arrive 1-3 months after period end; capital calls and K-1 UBTI follow.

complexity_challenge: Accept fewer illiquid structures; when held, a quarterly lag policy is enough.
automation_rationale: Roll-forward arithmetic deterministic; valuation judgment human.
analogy_breaks_down: Donor's business interest raises §4943/4958 issues absent in endowments.
evidence: https://coloradogivesfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Colorado-Gives-Foundation-December-31-2025-Audited-Financial-Statement-Final.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23): Note 2 Investments: alternatives 'reported at fair value when statements are received, which may have a lag of one to three months'; Note 4 NAV practical expedient investments 'are not classified in the fair value hierarchy'

capability: Crypto contributions and holdings across a reporting date
business_problem: Crypto received may be held briefly or long; ASU 2023-08 changes measurement.
why_industry_requires: Asset managers/custodians handle 24/7 pricing and principal market.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Most sponsors liquidate on receipt via a broker; if any crypto is held at period end, ASU 2023-08 fair value and separate presentation apply.
complexity_challenge: Prefer liquidate-on-receipt through a specialist; then only the exposure window and timestamp matter.
automation_risks: Holding over period-end measured at cost.
analogy_breaks_down: No custody of keys by sponsor if broker-liquidated.

NFPs for fiscal years beginning after Dec 15, 2024

automation_risks: Wrong level for thinly traded bonds.

capability: Tax-lot accounting for a tax-exempt sponsor
business_problem: Is lot tracking needed when the sponsor pays no capital-gains tax?
why_industry_requires: Taxable wealth clients need lots for gains tax.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Needed only for (a) Form 8282 disposition linkage, (b) §4943 holdings, (c) UBTI on S-corp stock/debt-financed property (carryover basis), (d) GAAP realized/unrealized split if presented. Not needed for most pooled assets.
complexity_challenge: Scope down: gift-lot identity everywhere; cost basis only for UBTI-tagged holdings.
automation_risks: Over-engineering lot relief methods for pools.
validation_evidence_needed: CPA confirmation that realized/unrealized split is not required in presentation.
analogy_breaks_down: Donor's basis is irrelevant to the sponsor's GAAP carrying amount (fair value at gift).

capability: UBTI-generating holdings and Form 990-T allocation

daf_equivalent_explanation: FI-37/TVF-192 cover priority of tax charges; tagging, carryover basis and allocation basis are missing.
complexity_challenge: Block S-corp stock acceptance by default; accept only with counsel rule.
automation_rationale: Tagging deterministic; tax computation by CPA.
automation_risks: Tax absorbed by sponsor operating fund without policy.
analogy_breaks_down: None.
