daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-025 specifies read-only IVR, numeric references, neutral responses; RCD-008 recommends deferral.
complexity_challenge: Defer until demand is evidenced (RCD-008); proactive status notices remove most status calls first.
automation_rationale: Lookup and disclosure rules are deterministic.
analogy_breaks_down: Insurers and carriers use IVR for very high volumes; DAF sponsors may not reach the volume that justifies it.

capability: Secure authenticated messaging
business_problem: Email is unauthenticated and unsuitable for account-specific detail; staff need a two-way channel bound to identity.
why_industry_requires: Banks and insurers use in-portal secure messaging to avoid disclosing PII by email.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-REM-005 lists secure message delivery; REQ-X-026 covers grant-scoped conversations only, not general service messages.
complexity_challenge: Generalize REQ-X-026 thread model to any subject (account, contribution, case) rather than adding a second messaging system.
automation_risks: Thread visible to wrong participant in multi-advisor funds.
validation_evidence_needed: Usability test with donors and charities.
analogy_breaks_down: None material; the pattern transfers directly.

capability: Caller identification and authentication assurance in assisted channels
business_problem: Social engineering of support is the cheapest account-takeover path (TVF-132).
why_industry_requires: Contact centers distinguish knowledge-based factors (weak, data-broker-knowable) from possession factors (OTP to registered device, in-app push).
daf_equivalent_explanation: TVF-132 open; UNB-RCN-ENT-016 requires verified-channel confirmation of staff-entered actions; IVR open decision 4 leaves disclosure-by-role undecided. No matrix of what may be disclosed or done at each assurance level per channel.
complexity_challenge: One matrix (channel x assurance x action class) replaces scattered per-workflow rules.
automation_rationale: Assurance level and permitted action are table lookups.
automation_risks: Staff override of matrix under caller pressure.
validation_evidence_needed: Penetration test of support desk with synthetic callers.
analogy_breaks_down: Banks have regulatory authentication guidance; DAF sponsors are charities, so the driver is fiduciary loss prevention, not a banking rule.

capability: Account-specific routing of contacts
business_problem: High-value or advisor-distributed accounts expect a known contact.
why_industry_requires: Private banking and premium insurance lines route to a named relationship manager.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-048 StickyAccountOwner routes back-office work; real-time contact routing to an owner who may be unavailable is not addressed.
complexity_challenge: For real-time calls, route to any qualified agent and create an owner follow-up task; only asynchronous messages should wait for the owner.
validation_evidence_needed: Sponsor contract SLAs for named-owner service.
analogy_breaks_down: Contact-center skills routing optimizes wait time at large pools; DAF pools are tiny, so sticky routing would destroy response time.

capability: Distinction between contact, case, financial transaction and operational exception
business_problem: Treating every contact as a case inflates queues; treating transactions as cases duplicates state machines.
why_industry_requires: Mature contact centers separate interaction records from cases from back-office transactions.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Requirements use case, WorkItem, WorkCase, ExceptionCase and service request interchangeably (RCF-PLT-025); no rule says when a contact becomes a case.
complexity_challenge: Four record types with explicit promotion rules; one shared case kernel; transactions keep their own aggregates.
automation_rationale: Promotion rules are deterministic (needs human response or follow-up -> case).
automation_risks: AI misclassification of an instruction as an inquiry.
validation_evidence_needed: Classify a synthetic month of contacts and measure promotion rate.
analogy_breaks_down: Telco/retail use separate CRM, ticketing and billing products; in a monolith the separation is a type boundary, not a system boundary.

capability: Case management for service requests
business_problem: Multi-step donor requests need durable ownership and status.
why_industry_requires: Ticketing systems give every non-trivial request an owner and status.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-015/016, AIN-009, REQ-X-048 cover; duplication noted in RCF-PLT-025.
complexity_challenge: Merge models (see XCAP-SVC-030).
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: SLA clocks with business calendars, pause and stop rules
business_problem: Overdue work is only measurable if clock start, pause and stop are defined.
why_industry_requires: Contact centers and regulated complaint regimes define clock semantics precisely.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-033 names SLAs, escalation and holidays; REQ-X-071 asks for 'exact clock definitions' but none are given; ADV-666 notes sponsor holiday risk.
complexity_challenge: Define three clock kinds only (response, resolution, decision) with a shared calendar engine.
automation_risks: Pause-abuse: clocks paused 'waiting for customer' without a real request.
validation_evidence_needed: Replay a year of synthetic cases across holiday calendars.
analogy_breaks_down: Regulatory complaint clocks (e.g. CFPB 15/60 days) are imposed on firms; DAF clocks are sponsor commitments, not law.

capability: Escalation (functional and hierarchical)
business_problem: Issues needing authority or expertise must reach the right person fast.
why_industry_requires: Tiered support (T1/T2/T3) is standard.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-046, UNB-GEX-005, landscape T0-T3 tiers.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Interaction recording and recording consent
business_problem: Recordings are needed for QA, dispute evidence and fraud investigation but are unlawful without required consent in all-party consent states.
why_industry_requires: Federal law permits one-party consent (18 USC 2511(2)(d)); states such as California and Florida require all parties' consent.
daf_equivalent_explanation: IVR spec says recordings require legal review before activation; TEL-01 retention is TBD; no consent capture requirement exists.
complexity_challenge: Simplest compliant design: announce and obtain consent on every recorded call nationwide; offer an unrecorded path; do not attempt per-state logic.
automation_rationale: Consent prompt and recording switch are deterministic.
automation_risks: Caller location unknown, so per-state logic fails; AI transcription vendor may be treated as a third-party interceptor.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel review of recording, transcription vendor terms and retention.
analogy_breaks_down: Insurers record for claims evidence; a DAF does not need recordings as primary evidence because instructions are taken through authenticated affirmation (UNB-RCN-GRT-010).
evidence: https://ktslaw.com/en/Blog/GlobalPrivacy-and-CybersecurityLaw/2024/7/Wiretap-Laws-in-the-United-States (search-result summary only; page not fully read) (accessed 2026-11-23)

capability: Transcription and AI interaction summaries
business_problem: Summaries reduce after-call work and preserve context.
why_industry_requires: Contact centers increasingly auto-summarize calls.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Only ADV-376 (IVR transcript documenting payment decision) touches it.
complexity_challenge: Summaries are notes, never instructions; avoids a new evidence class.
automation_risks: Hallucinated commitments or instructions in summary.
analogy_breaks_down: In insurance a recorded statement can be evidence; in a DAF a transcript must not become a grant instruction.

capability: Sentiment, intent and complaint signal detection
business_problem: Complaints are often not labeled as complaints by the customer.
why_industry_requires: Complaint regimes expect firms to recognize expressions of dissatisfaction.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Landscape proposes a sentiment and complaint classifier that may add but never clear flags; no Unbound requirement.
complexity_challenge: Flag-only classifier with human confirmation; never route money or authority on sentiment.
automation_risks: False negatives hide complaints; bias across languages.
validation_evidence_needed: Labelled synthetic contact set; precision/recall by language.
analogy_breaks_down: Sentiment-based routing optimizes retention in commerce; here it may only add a review flag.

capability: Knowledge management with governed answer corpus
business_problem: Staff and AI must give consistent, correct policy answers.
why_industry_requires: Contact centers maintain versioned knowledge bases; regulated firms approve customer-facing language.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-053 covers contextual AI guidance for configuration and staff; landscape requires answer corpus with clause IDs; no Unbound requirement versions donor-facing answers.
complexity_challenge: One corpus with clause IDs reused by help pages, staff scripts and AI answers.
automation_rationale: Corpus authoring is human; retrieval and citation checking deterministic plus AI.
automation_risks: Ungrounded AI answer creating misleading statement exposure.
validation_evidence_needed: Validator pass rate on synthetic question set.
analogy_breaks_down: Commerce knowledge bases are marketing-owned; DAF answers touch tax and exclusive legal control, so counsel approval of clauses is needed.

capability: Quality assurance sampling
business_problem: Measures answer accuracy and policy compliance.
why_industry_requires: QA scoring of a sample of interactions is standard.
daf_equivalent_explanation: CTL-040 names service QA sampling and complaint taxonomy with QA scores and inter-rater checks but no sample design.
complexity_challenge: Stratified small samples plus AI pre-scoring with human review of disagreements.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Supervisor oversight
business_problem: Supervisors need workload, SLA risk and override visibility.
why_industry_requires: Contact centers use real-time wallboards, barge/whisper.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-049 Supervisor Command Center; RCD-026 recommends exception-first workbench.
complexity_challenge: Real-time barge/whisper and wallboards are unnecessary at DAF volume; keep asynchronous oversight.
analogy_breaks_down: Real-time supervision presumes dozens of concurrent agents.

capability: Workforce management and surge staffing (Erlang-C for real-time channels)
business_problem: December giving surge and December 31 deadline concentrate time-critical contacts.
why_industry_requires: WFM forecasts arrivals by interval and sizes agents to a service level with Erlang-C/A.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Economic model sizes deferrable exception backlog for December (k multiplier) but has no real-time channel model; TVC-017 notes the surge is absent from staffing.
complexity_challenge: Convert real-time demand to deferrable (scheduled callbacks, async messages) to escape small-pool Erlang penalties.
automation_rationale: Queueing math is deterministic; forecast inputs are estimates.
automation_risks: Under-forecast on deadline days causes abandonment and missed year-end gifts.
analogy_breaks_down: Large contact centers have pooled agents; small sponsors cannot pool, so occupancy at service level is low and cost per contact high.

capability: Follow-up commitment tracking
business_problem: Broken promises ('we will call you by Friday') are a leading complaint cause.
why_industry_requires: Contact centers track callbacks and promised actions with due dates.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-024 notes include follow-up references; no typed commitment with due date or breach escalation.
complexity_challenge: A Commitment is a small typed child of Contact or Case with due date and owner; reuse SLA engine.
automation_risks: Commitments recorded only in free-text notes.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Complaint management
business_problem: Complaints need recognition, acknowledgement, investigation, response and root-cause learning; regulator/AG complaints carry legal risk.
why_industry_requires: Complaint handling is mandated in banking/insurance; regulators track response times (CFPB: generally 15 days, final 60).
daf_equivalent_explanation: WF-09 complaint flow, AUA-07, UNB-REM-006, CTL-040 taxonomy; no definition of complaint, no response clocks, no regulator-origin handling.
complexity_challenge: Use the case kernel with a complaint profile; no separate complaint system.
automation_rationale: Recognition AI-assisted; clocks deterministic; resolution human.
validation_evidence_needed: Complaint corpus by denominator (exists in landscape).
analogy_breaks_down: DAF sponsors are charities generally outside CFPB complaint jurisdiction; state AGs and IRS are the practical escalation venues.

capability: Dispute resolution among participants
business_problem: Conflicting instructions between co-advisors or successors must hold consequential actions.
why_industry_requires: Account disputes freeze activity in banking.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-023, UNB-RCN-ENT-008.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: CSAT, NPS and customer effort measurement
business_problem: Service quality must be measured without biased denominators.
why_industry_requires: Contact centers survey CSAT/CES post-contact and NPS relationally.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-042 names user effort, time to resolution, repeated contacts and outcome without definitions.
complexity_challenge: Measure repeat contact and outcome from system data first; surveys second.
analogy_breaks_down: NPS relational benchmarks are retail; donors have low switching, so NPS is weak signal.

capability: AI-assisted resolution (agent assist)
business_problem: Staff need context, draft replies and next actions.
why_industry_requires: Agent-assist is mainstream in contact centers.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Autonomous AI resolution of informational contacts
business_problem: Most status and how-to questions need no person.
why_industry_requires: Chatbots/voicebots resolve tier-1 questions.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Landscape T1 answer agent read-only; Unbound AIN-003 limits authority; no Unbound requirement for answer validation against state/corpus.
complexity_challenge: Proactive state notices first; autonomous answers only for informational intents with claim-to-citation validator.
automation_risks: Misleading statements; disclosure of screening logic.
validation_evidence_needed: Validator pass-rate and QA accuracy targets (landscape H §16).
analogy_breaks_down: Commercial bots may sell; a DAF bot must never imply donor control of assets.

capability: Proactive notification to prevent contacts
business_problem: 'Where is my grant' is the dominant status contact.
why_industry_requires: Logistics and insurers send proactive status to cut inbound volume.
daf_equivalent_explanation: AIN-030, UNB-RCN-PLT-002, landscape event triggers.
complexity_challenge: Highest-leverage deflection lever; prioritize before IVR or bots.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Vulnerable customer and accessibility accommodation
business_problem: Older or impaired donors need alternate channels and representatives.
why_industry_requires: Regulated firms maintain vulnerability flags and accommodations.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-045, AIN-024; no protective refusal of a suspected abusive representative.
complexity_challenge: See XCAP-CLM-020.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Repeat contact and first-contact resolution measurement
business_problem: Repeat contacts reveal unresolved root causes.
why_industry_requires: FCR is a core contact-center KPI.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-042 mentions repeated contacts only.
complexity_challenge: Define repeat = same principal + same reason within 7 calendar days.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Contact history retention and records class
business_problem: Recordings, transcripts and messages need retention classes and holds.
why_industry_requires: Firms retain recordings by regulation or policy.
daf_equivalent_explanation: TEL-01 TBD; RR-REQ-X-036-r1 retention catalog.
complexity_challenge: Classify by content (instruction evidence vs ordinary service) not by channel.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Multilingual service
business_problem: Sponsors serve diverse donors.
why_industry_requires: Contact centers route by language.
daf_equivalent_explanation: IVR spec multilingual prompts per sponsor; corpus translation not addressed.
complexity_challenge: Translate governed clauses, not free answers.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

industry: Legal case management / BPO / case-based fraud investigation
capability: Business process outsourcing of servicing
business_problem: Outsourced-admin and white-label sponsors use third-party service staff.
why_industry_requires: BPOs operate client contact centers under client rules and QA.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-073 vendor assurance (SOC) and ADM-026 partner service boundaries; no vendor-staff principal scoping, per-vendor QA or offboarding requirement.
complexity_challenge: Model vendor staff as a principal type with permitted action set rather than a separate portal.
analogy_breaks_down: BPO labor arbitrage matters less when contact volume is low.

industry: Legal case management / BPO / case-based fraud investigation
capability: Case-based fraud investigation confidentiality
business_problem: Investigations must not tip off subjects; investigators must not adjudicate.
why_industry_requires: Insurer SIUs and bank investigation units restrict case visibility and separate investigation from decision.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-GEX-033 escalates suspected fraud; IVR forbids disclosing investigative notes; no restricted case kind or investigator/adjudicator separation.
complexity_challenge: Restricted access class on the case kernel; no separate investigation system.
automation_risks: Leakage via service staff or AI assistant.
analogy_breaks_down: SAR confidentiality (BSA) generally does not bind charities; confidentiality here is policy and litigation prudence.

capability: Unified work management kernel
business_problem: One case/work model across grants, contributions, vetting, complaints, financial exceptions and compliance investigations.
why_industry_requires: Enterprises with many ticketing tools lose items between them.
daf_equivalent_explanation: RCF-PLT-025 finds five models and proposes one aggregate with one lifecycle; RR-REQ-X-057-r1 requires one case model. Shared lifecycle couples SLA clocks, permissions and holds.
complexity_challenge: Kernel shared (identity, links, ownership, routing, timeline, audit); policy per case kind (clock, access, retention/hold, outcomes, independence, closure rule).
validation_evidence_needed: Model five case kinds against kernel; count kind-specific exceptions.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Intake with completeness and duplicate detection
business_problem: Incomplete or duplicate submissions waste reviewer time.
why_industry_requires: First notice of loss captures required data and detects duplicates.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant intake, EXC-10 duplicate/split grants, idempotency.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Eligibility determination by versioned rules
business_problem: Coverage/eligibility must be decided consistently.
why_industry_requires: Claims systems apply policy rules at decision time.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-007, RR-REQ-X-007-r1, tiered decision architecture.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Insurance eligibility is contractual; DAF eligibility is statutory (§4966) plus sponsor policy.

capability: Evidence collection and information requests (RFI) with deadlines
business_problem: Pended cases stall indefinitely without RFI deadlines and auto-disposition.
why_industry_requires: Claims and prior authorization pend for information with deadlines and close as incomplete.
daf_equivalent_explanation: AIN-007 asks only for missing data and reuses verified evidence; REQ-X-048 WaitingForEvidence; no RFI deadline, reminder, tolling or auto-disposition.
complexity_challenge: One RFI object with due date and outcome; reuse evidence registry before asking.
automation_risks: Repeated asks for documents already held.
validation_evidence_needed: Count of duplicate asks in pilot.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Historical decision reconstruction (rules as of decision date)
business_problem: Auditors and appeals need what rules and facts applied at the time.
why_industry_requires: Claims re-review uses policy form and rule version in force at date of loss/decision.
daf_equivalent_explanation: TVR-DATA-001 as-known-at reconstruction; PPE G16 historical audit gate; ADV-015 version pinning; UNB-SUCC-012.
complexity_challenge: Do not mandate event sourcing; reconstructability suffices (TVF-065).
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Adjudication with specific reason codes
business_problem: Unexplained denials generate complaints and appeals.
why_industry_requires: NAIC Model 900 Sec.4(L) requires reasonable explanation of denials; ERISA 2560.503-1(g) requires specific reasons and rules relied on; CMS-0057-F requires specific denial reasons.
daf_equivalent_explanation: AIN-025 explains blocked decisions; PPE gates produce reason codes; no catalog of donor/charity-facing decline reasons or notice content.
complexity_challenge: Reuse gate outcome codes as the reason catalog; map each to public wording.
analogy_breaks_down: Insurers owe contractual duties to claimants; sponsors owe no duty to approve a recommendation, but fairness and complaint reduction still favor reasons.

capability: Fraud detection and special investigations (SIU)
business_problem: Fraudulent payees, diverted grants and account takeover.
why_industry_requires: Insurers run SIUs with referral rules and investigation separate from adjudication.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-072 fraud signals and holds; UNB-GEX-033; restricted investigation case missing.
complexity_challenge: Referral rules deterministic; investigation human; holds owned by domain.
analogy_breaks_down: Insurer fraud is claimant-driven; DAF fraud is mostly takeover and payee diversion.

capability: Case ownership and human escalation
business_problem: See XCAP-SVC-007/009.
why_industry_requires: Adjusters own files cradle-to-grave.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-048 CradleToGrave.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Exception processing
business_problem: Non-standard claims route to specialists.
why_industry_requires: Exception desks.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-041, UNB-GEX-*.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Appeals and reconsideration with independent review
business_problem: Adverse decisions need a fair, timely second look by someone other than the original decider.
why_industry_requires: ERISA requires review not deferring to the initial decision, by a fiduciary neither the original decider nor subordinate, and decision deadlines.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-RCN-ENT-016 requires a reconsideration case with outcome set, owner and response time, but not independence, de novo review, filing window or what new evidence is considered.
complexity_challenge: One reconsideration profile on the case kernel; no external review body.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel view on exclusive legal control.
analogy_breaks_down: ERISA appeals are a statutory right with litigation behind them; DAF reconsideration is discretionary courtesy because the sponsor holds exclusive legal control.

capability: Payment authorization separated from adjudication
business_problem: Approval of a claim is not authority to pay.
why_industry_requires: Claims payment authority limits and dual control.
daf_equivalent_explanation: CTL-003 payment gate; UNB-GEX-025; REQ-X-083.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Case reopening
business_problem: New facts after closure must be handled without rewriting history.
why_industry_requires: Claims reopen files for supplements or recoveries.
daf_equivalent_explanation: SM-0 forbids reopening terminal objects (child record); UNB-GEX-023 and EXC-18 speak of reopened cases. Rule needed: decisions never reopen; work cases may reopen with versioned history.
complexity_challenge: Decision aggregates: child records. Work cases: reopen allowed within window, else new linked case.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Decision notifications
business_problem: Claimants need timely notice of outcome and options.
why_industry_requires: Mandatory notice content in claims/health.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-RCN-PLT-002 notification catalog; content of adverse notice missing.
complexity_challenge: Template per reason code.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Closed-file decision-quality audit (leakage review)
business_problem: Straight-through approvals can contain undetected errors.
why_industry_requires: Insurers audit closed claims for leakage.
daf_equivalent_explanation: CTL-040 samples service; UNB-GEX-023 tracks false positives of exceptions; nothing samples automated approvals for false negatives.
complexity_challenge: Small stratified sample of STP and human approvals reviewed independently.
automation_rationale: Sampling deterministic; review human with AI pre-check.
automation_risks: Sample too small to detect rare errors.
analogy_breaks_down: Leakage in insurance is money overpaid; in DAF the harm is a taxable distribution or ineligible grantee.

capability: Applying claims adjudication patterns to grant review
business_problem: Grant review can borrow intake, RFI, reason codes, independent appeal and leakage audit.
why_industry_requires: n/a
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant lifecycle already uses gates and holds; missing RFI deadlines, reason notices, independent reconsideration and leakage audit.
complexity_challenge: Adopt only those four patterns.
analogy_breaks_down: Claims have a claimant with contractual entitlement; a grant recommendation is advisory.

capability: Applying claims patterns to charity vetting
business_problem: Vetting is eligibility adjudication on a third party.
why_industry_requires: n/a
daf_equivalent_explanation: Shared vetting and freshness exist; charity-facing reason and reconsideration path missing (CHAR-ADR-007 only names appeals).
complexity_challenge: Charity reconsideration on shared vetting record, separate from sponsor grant decisions.
analogy_breaks_down: Charities are not claimants; they cannot demand a grant.

capability: Applying claims patterns to contribution acceptance
business_problem: Complex gift acceptance is adjudication of an offer.
why_industry_requires: n/a
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-010/011 contribution acceptance; reasons for declining a gift and RFI deadlines are not specified.
complexity_challenge: Reuse RFI and reason-code patterns.
analogy_breaks_down: Donor has no entitlement to acceptance.

capability: Eligibility verification with ex parte reuse
business_problem: Repeated asks for already-known facts frustrate customers.
why_industry_requires: Health plans verify eligibility electronically; Medicaid renewals reuse available data before contacting members.
daf_equivalent_explanation: AIN-007 reuse verified evidence; RR-REQ-X-007-r1 freshness; shared charity vetting.
complexity_challenge: Enforce pre-ask registry check (see XCAP-CLM-003).
analogy_breaks_down: Medicaid renewal rules are federal; analog only.

capability: Prior-authorization-style decision deadlines and published metrics
business_problem: Requesters need predictable decision time.
why_industry_requires: CMS-0057-F: 72 hours expedited, 7 calendar days standard, specific denial reasons, public metrics from 2026.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-033 SLAs; no per-decision-type decision-time commitment or published metrics.
complexity_challenge: Declare decision-time target per decision type in the SLA engine; publish p50/p90.
analogy_breaks_down: Health prior-auth deadlines are law for impacted payers; DAF deadlines would be voluntary commitments.

capability: External provider verification (credentialing/NPPES analog)
business_problem: Verifying an external organization once and reusing it.
why_industry_requires: Primary-source verification; NPI is an identifier, not a credential.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Shared charity registry; UNB-CHAR-016 absence is not ineligibility; EIN is identifier not eligibility.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: NPPES enumeration does not verify licensure (unverified - general knowledge); IRS BMF presence likewise does not prove current eligibility.

capability: Consent and delegated authority (personal representative)
business_problem: Representatives act for donors; scope and abuse must be controlled.
why_industry_requires: HIPAA 164.502(g): representative treated as individual only for information relevant to their authority; (g)(5) permits refusing recognition on reasonable belief of abuse/endangerment.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-005 scoped delegation; ADM-045 representatives without assuming incapacity; no protective refusal path.
complexity_challenge: Scope = permissions already in delegation model; add protective suspension.
analogy_breaks_down: HIPAA applies to covered entities; sponsors are not; this is design analogy only.

capability: Sensitive data access: minimum necessary and break-glass
business_problem: Staff should see only what the task requires.
why_industry_requires: HIPAA minimum necessary (164.502(b)).
daf_equivalent_explanation: Field-level authorization and restricted classes exist (REQ-X-024, IVR); minimum-necessary by task type not stated.
complexity_challenge: Task-type views on case kernel.
analogy_breaks_down: Analogy only.

capability: Audit trails
business_problem: Who saw/changed what.
why_industry_requires: HIPAA audit controls.
daf_equivalent_explanation: OPS-024, UNB-GEX-004, REQ-X-048 assignment audit.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Orchestration with elimination of handoffs
business_problem: Handoffs add latency and errors.
why_industry_requires: Prior auth automation aims for electronic end-to-end decisions.
daf_equivalent_explanation: RR-REQ-X-048-r1; UNB-RCN-PLT-006 STP metrics; W5.
complexity_challenge: Measure handoffs per outcome.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

industry: Legal case management / BPO / case-based fraud investigation
capability: Legal matter cases with privilege and legal hold
business_problem: Litigation and regulator inquiries require privilege protection and holds.
why_industry_requires: Legal matter management tags privileged material and preserves data.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-GAP-019 names legal holds; retention specs cover holds; privilege marking absent.
complexity_challenge: Privileged access class on kernel; holds bind subjects not cases.
automation_risks: Privileged notes exported to auditors or AI context.
analogy_breaks_down: Small sponsors rely on outside counsel; keep minimal.

capability: Claim reserves
business_problem: Insurers reserve expected cost per claim.
why_industry_requires: Statutory accounting.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant reservations/encumbrances already cover committed amounts; no need for actuarial reserves.
complexity_challenge: Do not add.
analogy_breaks_down: Insurance reserves estimate uncertain liabilities; DAF grant amounts are known.

capability: Recovery and subrogation
business_problem: Recover misdirected or returned funds.
why_industry_requires: Subrogation.
daf_equivalent_explanation: EXC-08 returned/recalled payments; UNB-RCN-GRT-016 recall.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Recurring eligibility review
business_problem: Eligibility decays.
why_industry_requires: Annual redeterminations.
daf_equivalent_explanation: RR-REQ-X-007-r1 freshness policy; UNB-RCN-GRT-014.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

industry: Legal case management / BPO / case-based fraud investigation
capability: Regulator and attorney-general inquiry handling
business_problem: Inquiries carry deadlines and legal risk.
why_industry_requires: Firms route regulator correspondence to compliance/legal with deadlines.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-GAP-019 compliance cases; landscape T3 covers AG complaints.
complexity_challenge: Complaint profile flag 'regulator-originated' routes to counsel.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Duplicate verification avoidance
business_problem: Requiring the same proof twice delays settlement.
why_industry_requires: NAIC Model 900 Sec.4(K) lists duplicate proof/verification as an unfair practice.
daf_equivalent_explanation: AIN-007 reuse; no enforcement that requests exclude held evidence.
complexity_challenge: Pre-ask registry check.
analogy_breaks_down: Unfair practice statutes apply to insurers only.

capability: Standard electronic request/response APIs for decisions
business_problem: Partners integrate decision status without phone calls.
why_industry_requires: CMS-0057-F requires Prior Authorization API.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-038 API-first; REQ-X-077 recipient interoperability.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Organization hierarchy (legal entity, program, cost center)
business_problem: Know which legal entity owns, acknowledges, bills and reports each activity.
why_industry_requires: ERP books are keyed by company code/entity; consolidation needs a strict hierarchy.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor/legal entity/partner/program/fund hierarchy exists (ADM-001, UNB-RCN-PLT-001). Cost centers are a sponsor-ERP concept and need not exist in Unbound.
complexity_challenge: Do not import ERP cost-center trees; carry only the dimensions DAF journals need (entity, program, fund, restriction) for export.
automation_rationale: Hierarchy is sponsor configuration, validated deterministically.
validation_evidence_needed: Fixture: two legal entities under one tenant; acknowledgment and fee journals carry the right entity.
analogy_breaks_down: ERP org trees model management accountability; DAF hierarchy models legal control (IRC 4966(d)(2)). Cost-center hierarchy has no legal meaning for fund assets.

capability: Procurement / purchasing
business_problem: Buy goods and services for sponsor operations with approvals and budget checks.
why_industry_requires: ERP procure-to-pay controls spend.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor operating procurement does not touch fund assets; it is an operating-finance function.
complexity_challenge: Exclude natively (RR-UNB-ACC-012-r1, RCD-013). Integration only: summarized journal export.
automation_risks: Scope creep into a sponsor ERP.
analogy_breaks_down: Procurement spends the sponsor's own unrestricted money; DAF assets cannot be spent on procurement at all.

capability: Vendor management and third-party risk (incl. SOC reports of vendors)
business_problem: Know which vendors process sponsor or donor data/money, their assurance, CUECs and exit plans.
why_industry_requires: SOC 1/2 reliance and subservice organizations are standard for regulated financial operations.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-073 lists topics (SOC scope, bridge letters, CUECs, subprocessors) but has no testable freshness or CUEC-mapping rule.
complexity_challenge: Keep a small critical-vendor register inside the evidence model; do not build a TPRM suite. Freshness and CUEC mapping are the only material controls.
automation_rationale: Report-period coverage and expiry are deterministic date math; reading a SOC report's exceptions is AI-assisted extraction with human sign-off.
automation_risks: AI misreads a qualified opinion or misses a subservice carve-out.
validation_evidence_needed: Synthetic SOC report metadata with gaps, a carve-out and an exception.
analogy_breaks_down: ERP vendor master is about paying vendors; DAF needs vendor assurance because vendors touch charitable assets and donor PII.

capability: Contract management (sponsor, partner, vendor, program agreements)
business_problem: Executed terms drive fees, responsibilities, data rights and exit.
why_industry_requires: ERP/CLM links obligations and pricing to executed contracts.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Account agreements (ADM-014) and partner contracts (REQ-X-064) exist; fee schedules are not required to cite the executed clause they implement.
complexity_challenge: No CLM product. Store executed agreement hash + structured terms only for clauses the platform enforces (fees, data rights, responsibilities).
automation_rationale: AI may extract candidate structured terms; a human approves (AG-03 equivalent in ontology).
automation_risks: Extraction error silently changes a fee.
validation_evidence_needed: Fee schedule activation blocked without approved clause link.
analogy_breaks_down: CLM manages negotiation lifecycle; Unbound needs only enforceable-term provenance.

capability: Accounts payable: sponsor operating expenses vs grant payables
business_problem: Pay vendors from operating funds and charities from DAF funds without crossing the two.
why_industry_requires: AP is one payee master and one payment run in an ERP.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant payables are native (UNB-ACC-007); operating AP is excluded (RR-UNB-ACC-012-r1). Nothing prevents a vendor payee being paid through the grant path or a charity-that-is-also-a-vendor being confused.
complexity_challenge: Keep two payee registries with a cross-match instead of one 'vendor master'. Simpler than unified AP and safer.
automation_rationale: Registry separation and EIN/bank cross-match are exact rules.
automation_risks: False matches on shared bank (fiscal sponsor) accounts.
validation_evidence_needed: Fixture: same EIN as vendor and grantee; vendor-only payee on grant.
analogy_breaks_down: In ERP AP every payee is fungible; in a DAF, a payment's legal character (grant vs expense) is fixed by the source fund and must not be inferred from the payee.

capability: Billing and accounts receivable
business_problem: Invoice partners/sponsors and collect platform fees; assess DAF admin fees.
why_industry_requires: ERP O2C/AR.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-ACC-010/013 say 'billing, collections' without distinguishing fund-deducted fees (no receivable), donor-paid membership fees, and partner/sponsor invoices.
complexity_challenge: Three payer types, three posting patterns; only partner invoices need AR.
automation_rationale: Fee computation and posting are reproducible math.
automation_risks: Charging fees to fund that should be invoiced to partner.
analogy_breaks_down: ERP AR assumes a customer who owes money; a DAF fund deducted for fees never owes anything.

capability: HR administration and workforce identity
business_problem: Know who is employed, in which role, to drive access and approval rights.
why_industry_requires: HRIS is source of truth for joiner/mover/leaver.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Only authority consequences matter: GOV-AUTH-025 and GOV-AUTH-015 require revocation on departure.
complexity_challenge: Integration only (SCIM/IdP). No native HR.
automation_risks: Stale HR feed leaves approver active.
analogy_breaks_down: HR manages employment; Unbound only consumes workforce status as an authority input.

capability: Role-based access control
business_problem: Least-privilege access per role and scope.
why_industry_requires: Standard ERP SoD.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Extensively covered (GOV-AUTH-001..026, UNB-ADV-002, UNB-PART-006, AUTH-I1..I8).
complexity_challenge: None needed.
analogy_breaks_down: ERP roles are job-function bundles; DAF roles are relationship-scoped per fund.

capability: Delegation-of-authority matrix and approval limits
business_problem: Approvers act within monetary and type limits; splitting a payment to stay under a limit is detected.
why_industry_requires: DoA matrices with cumulative limits are core ERP and banking controls.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Decision-rights matrix and GOV-AUTH-001 exist; 'amount threshold splitting' is only a listed test with no aggregation rule.
complexity_challenge: One aggregation rule (approver x counterparty x window) is enough; avoid per-sponsor bespoke formulas.
automation_risks: Window too short lets structuring pass.
validation_evidence_needed: Fixture: three approvals at 90% of limit to one payee in 5 days.
analogy_breaks_down: ERP limits are per document; DAF grants are per fund and per recipient and may be legitimately split across funds (ONT-4).

capability: Task management / work queues
business_problem: Route work with owner, SLA and authority.
why_industry_requires: ERP workflow inboxes.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-031, ADM-016 and the work-queue specification cover it.
complexity_challenge: None.
automation_rationale: Routing is deterministic; triage summaries AI-assisted.
analogy_breaks_down: Departmental inbox model was rejected (ontology DD-013).

capability: Budgeting and forecasting
business_problem: Plan sponsor operating spend.
why_industry_requires: ERP planning.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor operating budget is not DAF administration (RCF-FIN-008).
complexity_challenge: Exclude; export actuals.
analogy_breaks_down: Fund balances are not budgets; donors are not budget holders.

capability: Resource allocation / cost-to-serve attribution
business_problem: Know what servicing a segment costs to price programs and partner agreements.
why_industry_requires: Activity-based costing in ERP/PSA.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM business metrics name 'cost to serve' and UNB-RCN-PLT-006 measures touches, but work items do not carry segment/program dimensions or effort.
complexity_challenge: Capture effort category and dimensions on work items; no timesheets.
automation_rationale: Dimensions copied from subject; effort from queue timestamps.
validation_evidence_needed: Compare against a sample of staff time logs.
analogy_breaks_down: ERP allocates cost to cost centers; here cost must be attributable to fund/program to inform fee setting, without charging funds for servicing outside the fee schedule.

capability: Operational analytics
business_problem: Throughput, backlog, SLA, exceptions.
why_industry_requires: ERP BI.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-047, UNB-RCN-PLT-006, work queue dashboards.
complexity_challenge: None.

capability: Internal controls (ICFR) and control evidence
business_problem: Prove controls operated.
why_industry_requires: SOX/ICFR.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Control matrix, SOC2 directive, UNB-SCTRL family; SOC 1 scope gap known (RCF-PLT-036).
complexity_challenge: None beyond known gaps.
analogy_breaks_down: Nonprofit sponsors are not SOX issuers; SOC 1 is the relevant analog for service orgs.

capability: Document retention
business_problem: Retain and dispose records lawfully.
why_industry_requires: Records management.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Classification matrix with 7-year financial floor, holds.
complexity_challenge: None; COM-03 marketing consent retention still TBD.
automation_rationale: Deterministic classification; AI suggestions never shorten.

capability: Multi-entity operations and intercompany
business_problem: Several legal entities share staff/platform; intercompany charges.
why_industry_requires: ERP intercompany.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-ACC-015 and UNB-RCN-PLT-001 cover entity distinction; platform-operator billing to sponsors is not separated from sponsor books.
complexity_challenge: Operator's own revenue never posts in tenant books.
analogy_breaks_down: ERP intercompany assumes common control; operator and sponsor are unrelated (or related-party) entities.

capability: Fee/billing event classification (financial vs informational)
business_problem: Event consumers must know which fee events are authoritative.
why_industry_requires: ERP distinguishes posted documents from notifications.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Fee lifecycle in ontology (accrual -> assessment -> posting -> collection -> refund) but no event classification.
complexity_challenge: One class attribute per event type.
automation_risks: CRM projection originating a fee change.

capability: Tiered fee schedules (marginal vs whole-balance)
business_problem: Compute admin fees on tiers.
why_industry_requires: Subscription/AUM billing.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-RCN-FIN-005 declares tier method; published sponsor schedules are marginal (0.60% first $500k, 0.30% next...).
complexity_challenge: None.

capability: Minimum fees and low-balance treatment
business_problem: Minimum annual fee may exceed small balances.
why_industry_requires: Subscription minimums.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-RCN-FIN-005 names minimums but not the case minimum > available balance, nor minimum proration.
complexity_challenge: Cap at available net of reservations; never a receivable.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS minimums create receivables; a DAF cannot bill the donor for a shortfall after the gift is complete.

capability: Proration and billing-period segmentation
business_problem: Open/close/transfer/schedule change mid-period.
why_industry_requires: Subscription proration.
daf_equivalent_explanation: No rule; TVS-308 shows migration double charge.
complexity_challenge: Daily accrual with declared day-count removes most proration edge cases.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS proration is credit-based; DAF must never refund to donor (UNB-RCN-FIN-013), so over-collection is re-credited to the fund.

capability: Donor-paid membership fees (flat subscription)
business_problem: Some challengers charge monthly membership to a card.
why_industry_requires: Consumer subscription.
daf_equivalent_explanation: No payer-source concept.
complexity_challenge: Treat as non-charitable payment for services outside the fund ledger.
analogy_breaks_down: Subscription revenue is ordinary; a payment to a charity sponsor by a donor may be confused with a contribution.

capability: White-label sponsor platform fees
business_problem: Operator charges sponsor SaaS/implementation/bps fees.
why_industry_requires: B2B SaaS billing.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-067 waterfall; operator-vs-sponsor book separation missing.
complexity_challenge: Operator billing in operator's own system.
analogy_breaks_down: Platform fee is the operator's revenue but often funded from sponsor admin-fee revenue (RCF paid Ren 95-98%).

capability: Unified party model with distinct roles
business_problem: One person/org may be donor, advisor, charity officer, staff.
why_industry_requires: CRM account/contact with roles.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ONT-1 and RR-UNB-PART-003-r1 adopt capacities as edges.
complexity_challenge: Keep identity core minimal; partition PII by capacity.
analogy_breaks_down: CRM '360 view' is the goal in sales; in a DAF it is a privacy and conflict hazard.

capability: Donor households
business_problem: Group family members for display and service.
why_industry_requires: CRM households.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-008/ONT-2: presentation only, no access.
complexity_challenge: Do not let households drive pricing or access.
analogy_breaks_down: CRM householding aggregates for pricing breakpoints; a DAF household cannot aggregate rights.

capability: Financial advisors and professional referral networks
business_problem: Advisor-led distribution and referrals.
why_industry_requires: Wealth CRM, referral tracking.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-062 covers advisor access/compensation; referral attribution and referral compensation are not.
complexity_challenge: Record attribution as fact; block compensation pending counsel.
analogy_breaks_down: Sales referral fees are ordinary; paying for charitable contributions can trigger paid-solicitor regimes.

capability: Prospects and sales pipeline
business_problem: Track potential donors/sponsors through stages.
why_industry_requires: CRM opportunity pipeline.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Donor prospect = draft establishment (ADM-002, UX-S09). B2B sponsor pipeline is the operator's own CRM.
complexity_challenge: No native pipeline; abandoned intake purged per TMP-01.
analogy_breaks_down: A DAF 'deal' has no revenue at close; value arises only on contribution acceptance.

capability: Institutional clients
business_problem: Banks, RIAs, employers, community foundations as clients.
why_industry_requires: B2B account management.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Tenant/partner/program entities.
complexity_challenge: None.

capability: Charitable organizations as relationships
business_problem: Charities are recipients, sometimes donors (organization-advised funds), vendors or partners.
why_industry_requires: CRM accounts with multiple relationship types.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Registry treats charities as recipients; charity-as-fund-holder and charity-affiliation edges (officer/employee of donor) are not captured as capacities.
complexity_challenge: Capacity edges on the same party core.
validation_evidence_needed: Fixture: church holds organization-advised fund and recommends grant to itself.
analogy_breaks_down: A CRM treats a charity as a customer; legally a charity recommending grants to itself from a fund it contributed is a different regime from a donor.

capability: Relationship ownership and servicing models
business_problem: Named relationship manager, coverage, backup.
why_industry_requires: CRM account owner.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Case ownership exists; fund-level servicing model/owner does not.
complexity_challenge: Owner is a routing attribute, never an access grant.

capability: Onboarding journeys
business_problem: Guided establishment.
why_industry_requires: CRM journeys.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-002, WF-01, UNB-PART-007.
complexity_challenge: None.

capability: Retention and attrition
business_problem: Detect and respond to outbound transfers and dormancy.
why_industry_requires: Churn models.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Outbound transfer and dormancy covered (UNB-RCN-ENT-005/007); retention outreach must not obstruct transfers.
complexity_challenge: Do not add win-back friction into a transfer workflow.
automation_rationale: Churn propensity is a model; actions are human.
automation_risks: Delay of a requested transfer for retention.
validation_evidence_needed: Transfer SLA unaffected by retention case.
analogy_breaks_down: A donor cannot 'take' the fund; transfer is a sponsor grant to another sponsor.

capability: Segmentation
business_problem: Group donors for communications and service.
why_industry_requires: Marketing segmentation.
daf_equivalent_explanation: No rule restricts segments derived from grant categories that reveal religion, health or politics.
complexity_challenge: Allowlist of segment attributes.
analogy_breaks_down: Purchase history segmentation is routine; grant history reveals protected beliefs.

capability: Campaigns and communications (CAN-SPAM, TCPA, consent)
business_problem: Send commercial and transactional messages lawfully across white-label senders.
why_industry_requires: Marketing automation compliance.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Notification catalog with consent basis (UNB-RCN-PLT-002) and template governance; sender-entity, opt-out and nonprofit-vs-for-profit sender regime missing.
complexity_challenge: Classify at the catalog; suppress at send.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel on CAN-SPAM applicability to sponsor messages.
analogy_breaks_down: CAN-SPAM covers commercial messages; TCPA has nonprofit-specific consent rules, so the legal regime depends on which entity is the sender.

capability: Relationship profitability
business_problem: Revenue and cost per fund/segment/partner.
why_industry_requires: CRM/ERP profitability.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-067 item 5 calls for profitability analytics; inputs missing (cost to serve).
complexity_challenge: Read-only analytics on posted fees + effort.
automation_risks: Profitability used to deprioritize grant processing for small funds.
analogy_breaks_down: Charitable assets are not the sponsor's customers' wallets; profitability may not alter legal service obligations.

capability: Service histories and lifecycle events
business_problem: Full interaction history.
why_industry_requires: CRM activity timeline.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Case history, documents, events.
complexity_challenge: None.

capability: External CRM synchronization (advisor/wealth CRM, charity CRM)
business_problem: Push state to Salesforce/Redtail/charity CRMs.
why_industry_requires: CRM integration.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-062 webhooks; REQ-X-077 recipient attribution; inbound CRM data must never be authoritative.
complexity_challenge: Outbound projections only; inbound edits become requests.

capability: Professional advisor change of firm
business_problem: Advisor moves firms; who keeps the relationship.
why_industry_requires: Wealth-management book transfer.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Not addressed.
complexity_challenge: Scope relationship to (individual, firm).
analogy_breaks_down: Broker protocol moves client accounts; DAF assets do not move with the advisor.

capability: Succession planning and successor advisors
business_problem: Continuity after death/incapacity.
why_industry_requires: Trust successor trustee provisions.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-SUCC-001..014 and refinements.
complexity_challenge: Generation and count caps vary (SVCF 3, CCT 2 generations): configuration, not code.
automation_rationale: Deterministic plan application; humans resolve disputes.
analogy_breaks_down: Trustee succession is fixed by instrument and state law; DAF successor rights are sponsor-policy privileges.

capability: Successor non-response and default disposition
business_problem: Named successor does not respond.
why_industry_requires: Trust administration timelines.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Dormancy lifecycle covers inactivity; post-death response window (Fidelity 90 days) not modeled.
complexity_challenge: One response-window parameter in the succession policy.

capability: Delegated authority (POA, guardians, executors)
business_problem: Representatives act for incapacitated principals.
why_industry_requires: Trust/estate fiduciary authority.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Representative subtypes in RR-UNB-PART-003-r1; whether a POA agent can exercise advisory privileges and how authority is restored are open.
complexity_challenge: Default deny unless instrument + policy.
analogy_breaks_down: POA covers property of the principal; DAF assets are not the principal's property.

capability: Conflicting instructions
business_problem: Co-advisors disagree; standing vs new instruction; plan versions.
why_industry_requires: Co-trustee deadlock rules.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-023 and UNB-PART-005 delegate to policy; AUTH-I4 defines 'require all' for successors only.
complexity_challenge: A fixed precedence table.
analogy_breaks_down: Co-trustees have fiduciary duties and courts; DAF co-advisors only recommend; the sponsor decides.

capability: Charitable beneficiaries and legacy intent
business_problem: Named charities at termination; letters of wishes.
why_industry_requires: Will/trust charitable remainder beneficiaries.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-SUCC-011 and ADM-018; no re-validation at activation; no legacy-letter record.
complexity_challenge: Validate at designation and activation; non-binding intent record.
analogy_breaks_down: Cy-pres applies to charitable trusts by court; DAF sponsors resolve by policy.

capability: Entity and trust holders
business_problem: Trust, LLC or corporation holds advisory privileges.
why_industry_requires: Entity signatory management.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Entity authorized signatory subtype exists; entity dissolution as trigger and signatory change as non-succession missing.
complexity_challenge: Treat entity as holder; signatories as delegated.

capability: Family governance and multigenerational participation
business_problem: Family councils, voting, minors.
why_industry_requires: Family office governance.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-PART-008, REQ-X-068.
complexity_challenge: Voting is advisory.
analogy_breaks_down: Family votes bind nothing.

capability: Historical decisions and reconstruction
business_problem: What was known when.
why_industry_requires: Trust accountings.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-SUCC-012, UNB-DATA-001.
complexity_challenge: None.

capability: Family consolidated reporting
business_problem: Family office wants one view across several funds and sponsors.
why_industry_requires: Family office consolidated reporting.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-044 cross-DAF views and UNB-RCN-ENT-013 export; no per-fund consent to consolidation.
complexity_challenge: Export feed; no native consolidation of non-Unbound assets.

capability: Account transfers (in/out, split, merge)
business_problem: Move funds between sponsors or split.
why_industry_requires: Trust decanting.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-RCN-ENT-007/008.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Decanting is trustee power; DAF transfer is a sponsor grant.

capability: Death and incapacity handling
business_problem: Verified events suspend authority.
why_industry_requires: Estate administration.
daf_equivalent_explanation: RR-UNB-SUCC-008-r1, UNB-RCN-ENT-004, AUTH-I3/I5.
complexity_challenge: Restoration after incapacity missing (see TRS-003).

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Charity status verification against IRS publications (Pub 78/EO BMF/Auto-Revocation List) with grant-date reliance snapshot
business_problem: Grantor must know recipient is a public charity on the grant date.
why_industry_requires: Private foundations rely on Rev. Proc. 2018-32 to avoid §4945 ER; DAF sponsors rely on it for the §4966(c)(2)(A) exception.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Identical reliance rule; DAF sponsor substitutes §4966 for §4945.
complexity_challenge: Not over-complicated once the 180-day deep review is treated as policy (already done in RR-REQ-X-007-r1). Keep the per-grant check deterministic and near-zero marginal cost.
automation_rationale: Monthly IRS files + rule; no judgment needed for listed §170(b)(1)(A) organizations.
automation_risks: Stale file treated as current; EIN/name mismatch.
validation_evidence_needed: Measured false-hold rate on BMF-listed recipients; source freshness logs.
analogy_breaks_down: Foundations often re-vet per grant manually; DAF volume (millions of grants) makes per-grant human vetting uneconomic.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Recipient identity resolution from free-text recommendations (name, EIN, address, IRC section variants)
business_problem: Donors and legacy data supply inconsistent names/EINs; payee must be the right legal entity.
why_industry_requires: Foundation grants managers match grantee to EIN before paying.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Same; DAF adds high volume and donor self-service entry.
complexity_challenge: Avoid free-text recipient entry: search-first selection from the registry removes most resolution work.
automation_rationale: Deterministic EIN match first; AI only to propose candidates for unmatched free text, never to confirm.
validation_evidence_needed: Precision/recall on a labelled sample such as the 20,000-line Schedule I sample.
analogy_breaks_down: Foundations have few, known grantees; DAF has a long tail of one-off recipients.
evidence: daf-landscape:data/charity-vetting-ai/resolution-eval-sample.csv (20,000 Schedule I lines; IRC section written '501(c)(3)', '501(C)3', '501 (C)(3)')

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Recipient-class eligibility mapping (Permitted / ERRequired / Prohibited / CounselReview)
business_problem: Determines whether a distribution is taxable.
why_industry_requires: PF practice maps grantee class to ER/no-ER under §4945.
daf_equivalent_explanation: DAF classes differ (§4966(d)(4) disqualified SOs; natural persons barred) and a 2026 temporary regulation adds a lawful 'natural-person-adjacent' route (§530A general funding contributions).
complexity_challenge: Class list is the right abstraction; add a versioned class for Treasury-administered §530A contributions rather than a human override.
automation_rationale: Classes derive from statute/regulation; mapping is a table.
automation_risks: Hard-coded class list cannot absorb new law (temp reg expires 2029-09-30).
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel sign-off on the class table including §1.530A-7T.
analogy_breaks_down: PF §4945 treats individual grants under (d)(3) with approval procedures; DAFs have no individual-grant route at all.
evidence: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-30/html/2026-20026.htm Temp. Reg. §1.530A-7T(e)(2)(i)-(ii) and (f) (DAF distribution as general funding contribution is not a §4966 natural-person distribution; treated as ER exercised; applies TY beginning on/after 2026-01-01; expires 2029-09-30) (accessed 2026-11-23)

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Charitable-purpose designations and restrictions on grants
business_problem: Donors want grants for a program; sponsor must avoid non-charitable or benefit-conferring purposes.
why_industry_requires: Foundations restrict grants and monitor use.
daf_equivalent_explanation: For DAF grants to §170(b)(1)(A) organizations, §4966(c)(2)(A) excepts the distribution regardless of stated purpose; restriction monitoring is policy, not law (except ER grants and the sponsor's own exempt-status limits, e.g. political campaign).
complexity_challenge: Over-complication risk: monitoring soft purpose designations to public charities adds cost without reducing §4966 exposure. Treat designations as communicated intent; reserve monitoring for ER and sponsor-elected restricted programs.
automation_rationale: Purpose text is screened by deterministic benefit catalogue; AI may raise Hold only.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel confirmation that §4966(c)(2)(A) applies irrespective of purpose for public-charity grantees, and of sponsor exempt-status limits.
analogy_breaks_down: Foundation restricted grants are contractual; DAF grants rarely carry agreements.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Delegated grant approval under board-adopted policy
business_problem: Approve millions of routine grants without per-grant officer review.
why_industry_requires: Foundations use board-delegated staff authority with dollar limits.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Same governance construct; OD-01 asks whether deterministic policy may hold the delegation.
complexity_challenge: None beyond OD-01.
analogy_breaks_down: Foundation volumes are small; DAF delegation is to a rule, not a person.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Grant agreements and award terms
business_problem: Bind grantee to purpose, repayment and reporting where needed.
why_industry_requires: Foundations issue signed agreements for most grants; ER requires a grantee-officer-signed commitment (§53.4945-5(b)(3)).
daf_equivalent_explanation: DAF routine grants to public charities need no signed agreement; unilateral award terms in remittance suffice as policy.
complexity_challenge: Do not import foundation-style agreements for every grant; tier: none (routine) / unilateral terms / signed agreement (ER, conditional, multi-year).
automation_rationale: Tier selection is a rule on recipient class and grant terms.
analogy_breaks_down: Foundation grant counts are small; agreement cost per DAF grant would dominate cost.
evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/53.4945-5 (b)(1), (b)(3) signed grantee commitment terms, (c) annual reports, (c)(3)(i) 4-year records, (a)(5) good faith determination (accessed 2026-11-23)

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Expenditure responsibility (pre-grant inquiry, signed agreement, annual reports, IRS reporting)
business_problem: Grants to non-excepted grantees must be policed.
why_industry_requires: §4945(h)/§53.4945-5 for PFs; incorporated for DAFs by §4966(c)(1)(B).
daf_equivalent_explanation: Mechanics transfer; NPRM would adopt §53.4945-5(b)-(e) with modifications.
complexity_challenge: Offer ER only where sponsor elects; most sponsor models can route to intermediaries instead.
automation_rationale: Deadlines/report tracking deterministic; report review human.
automation_risks: AI summarizing reports treated as verification.
analogy_breaks_down: PF ER is reported on Form 990-PF; DAF sponsor reporting channel is unsettled under the NPRM.
evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/53.4945-5 (b)(1), (b)(3) signed grantee commitment terms, (c) annual reports, (c)(3)(i) 4-year records, (a)(5) good faith determination (accessed 2026-11-23)

https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2023-11-14/html/2023-24982.htm preamble and proposed foreign-organization distributee paragraph (good faith determination using procedures similar to §53.4945-5(a)(5); foreign governments treated as §170(b)(1)(A) if exclusively public purposes) (accessed 2026-11-23)

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Equivalency determination (ED) for foreign grantees with currency tracking
business_problem: Treat a foreign organization as a public charity without ER.
why_industry_requires: PFs use §53.4945-5(a)(5) and Rev. Proc. 2017-53; shared ED repositories exist.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Rev. Proc. 2017-53 §2 expressly lets DAF sponsors use the guidelines for §4966(c)(2)(A) until further guidance.
complexity_challenge: Currency is computable (grantee taxable year of the facts + law-unchanged); no human needed to track expiry.
automation_rationale: Expiry deterministic; written-advice content review by qualified practitioner (human).
automation_risks: AI drafting an ED is not 'written advice from a qualified tax practitioner'.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel on reuse of advice procured by another grantor.
analogy_breaks_down: Domestic BMF reliance is publication-based; ED reliance is advice-based and expires.
evidence: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-17-53.pdf §2 (DAF sponsors may use guidelines for §4966(c)(2)(A)) and §4.02(1) (currency: up to two years tied to grantee taxable year) (accessed 2026-11-23)

https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2023-11-14/html/2023-24982.htm preamble and proposed foreign-organization distributee paragraph (good faith determination using procedures similar to §53.4945-5(a)(5); foreign governments treated as §170(b)(1)(A) if exclusively public purposes) (accessed 2026-11-23)

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: International giving via US intermediaries (CAF America, GlobalGiving, Give2Asia, 'friends of' organizations)
business_problem: Donors want foreign causes without sponsor-level ED/ER cost.
why_industry_requires: Community foundations commonly refer international grants to intermediaries.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant is to a domestic §170(b)(1)(A) organization, so routine path applies; intermediary must retain discretion.
complexity_challenge: Cheapest compliant path; avoids building ED/ER for sponsors that do not want it.
automation_rationale: Intermediary list and routing rule are configuration.
automation_risks: Earmarking language could make intermediary a conduit.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel on earmark wording in DAF context.
analogy_breaks_down: A PF using an intermediary is analysed under §53.4945-5(a)(6) earmarking; DAF analogue under §4966 is not settled.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Fiscal sponsorship handling (comprehensive vs pre-approved grant relationship)
business_problem: Projects without own exemption receive funds via a fiscal sponsor.
why_industry_requires: Foundations pay the fiscal sponsor, require evidence of the sponsorship agreement and that the sponsor controls funds.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Same legal payee logic; DAF must also avoid conduit payments to individuals or for-profits through a fiscal sponsor.
complexity_challenge: Separate facts exist; missing is typed evidence and a conduit test.
automation_rationale: Evidence presence deterministic; agreement interpretation human first time, then reusable.
automation_risks: Fiscal sponsor name on BMF passes check while project is a for-profit.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel on model types and conduit test.
analogy_breaks_down: Foundations handle few fiscal sponsors; DAF donors name projects directly.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Supporting-organization donor-control certification
business_problem: Type I/II/FI-III SO grants can be taxable if donor controls.
why_industry_requires: PFs use Notice 2006-109 reliance.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Notice 2014-4 §3.02 confirms sponsors may continue to rely on Notice 2006-109 §3.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: None material.
evidence: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/n-14-04.pdf §3.02 (sponsoring organizations may continue to rely on Notice 2006-109 §3 reliance standards until further guidance) (accessed 2026-11-23)

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Grantee reporting and outcomes
business_problem: Know what grants achieved; ER requires reports.
why_industry_requires: Foundations require narrative/financial reports.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Legally required only for ER grants; otherwise optional.
complexity_challenge: Keep optional outside ER to protect nonprofit burden.
automation_rationale: AI extracts report data; claims remain evidence.
analogy_breaks_down: Foundation reports tie to multi-year relationships; DAF grants are mostly one-off.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Sponsor information-return data: Form 990 Schedule I and Schedule F grant detail
business_problem: Sponsor must report grants >$5,000 per recipient (Schedule I) and foreign grants/activities (Schedule F: region, purpose, manner of disbursement, ED/ER procedures).
why_industry_requires: All grantmaking public charities file these schedules.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Identical obligation; DAF scale makes manual assembly expensive.
complexity_challenge: Capture at source on the grant record; aggregate per recipient per tax year.
automation_risks: Region/manner fields missing on legacy grants.
validation_evidence_needed: CPA mapping to current form lines.
analogy_breaks_down: None; this is the same filing.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Grantee notification and remittance communication
business_problem: Charity must know who sent funds and that the sponsor is the legal donor.
why_industry_requires: Foundations send award letters.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Covered by UNB-RCN-GRT-011 and REQ-X-077.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: DAF adds anonymity and advisor attribution.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Grantee acknowledgment / receipt collection
business_problem: Confirm receipt; avoid deductible receipts to donors.
why_industry_requires: Foundations often request receipts; ER needs reports, not receipts.
daf_equivalent_explanation: The sponsor needs no receipt for any deduction; settlement evidence proves payment. Acknowledgment is convention.
complexity_challenge: Make non-blocking; do not chase receipts.
analogy_breaks_down: Individual-donor receipts are §170(f)(8) driven; grantor receipts are not.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Donor recommendation intake with affirmations
business_problem: Recommendations must not create benefits; donor affirms.
why_industry_requires: Foundations do not have advisors; closest is board member requests.
daf_equivalent_explanation: DAF-specific.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: No PF equivalent of advisor privileges.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Recurring and future-dated grants
business_problem: Scheduled grants must be re-evaluated at each occurrence.
why_industry_requires: Multi-year foundation commitments with payment schedules.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Same; DAF occurrences are recommendations, not commitments.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Foundation multi-year grants are legal commitments (payables); DAF schedules are not.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Delivery: rail selection and destination evidence
business_problem: Pay the right account cheaply.
why_industry_requires: Foundations use ACH/check/wire.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Same.
complexity_challenge: Phase out checks (P09/P10 pools).
analogy_breaks_down: None.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Cancellation, refused and returned grants with re-credit
business_problem: Undelivered value must return to the fund with history.
why_industry_requires: Foundation returned grants revert to the foundation.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Re-credit to originating fund; no new acknowledgment.
complexity_challenge: None.
automation_risks: Re-credit to wrong fund after succession.
analogy_breaks_down: None.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Charity organizational change impact on open and recurring grants (merger, successor, name/EIN change, dissolution, bankruptcy, revocation, retroactive reinstatement)
business_problem: In-flight grants may be payable to an entity that no longer exists or is now a different legal person.
why_industry_requires: Foundations amend or reassign grants on grantee merger; returned grants on dissolution.
daf_equivalent_explanation: History is modelled (UNB-CHAR-004) but no deterministic per-event effect on open grants.
complexity_challenge: Most events (name change with same EIN) need no human; only successor-payee substitution needs sponsor approval.
automation_risks: Auto-substituting successor payee without approval enables diversion.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel on payee substitution and retroactive reinstatement (Rev. Proc. 2014-11).
analogy_breaks_down: Foundation grants are few; manual handling scales there.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Payee bank-account change fraud prevention
business_problem: BEC-style redirection of grant payments.
why_industry_requires: Universal AP control.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Same.
complexity_challenge: Duplicate statements flagged in RCF-GRT-030.
analogy_breaks_down: None.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Sponsor discretionary (non-legal) grant holds and declines
business_problem: Sponsors may decline lawful grants on policy/reputational grounds; regulators scrutinize consistency.
why_industry_requires: Foundations have full discretion over their own grants.
daf_equivalent_explanation: DAF sponsor discretion is legal (exclusive control) but now draws AG scrutiny (2026 multistate letter).
complexity_challenge: Need criteria, expiry and consistency evidence, not more review steps.
automation_rationale: Discretionary decisions are reserved to sponsor authority.
automation_risks: AI-generated allegation summaries treated as findings.
analogy_breaks_down: Foundation grants are the foundation's own choice; DAF donors expect recommendation honoured.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Uncashed grant checks and unclaimed-property reporting
business_problem: Stale checks are liabilities and may be reportable.
why_industry_requires: All holders.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Same; jurisdiction priority must be decided.
complexity_challenge: Phasing out checks removes most of the problem.
analogy_breaks_down: None.
evidence: https://www.iofm.com/ask-the-expert/handling-uncashed-donation-checks-and-escheatment (tax-exempt holders not exempt; secondary; search-result summary) (accessed 2026-11-23)

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Foreign-official / anti-bribery diligence for international grants
business_problem: Grants benefiting foreign officials can violate FCPA.
why_industry_requires: International foundations run anti-corruption diligence.
daf_equivalent_explanation: FCPA 'domestic concern' covers US-organized nonprofits.
complexity_challenge: One questionnaire field set at ED/ER intake, not a separate workflow.
analogy_breaks_down: Domestic grants have no analogue.

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: OFAC license basis for grants touching sanctioned jurisdictions
business_problem: Some humanitarian grants are authorized by general licenses.
why_industry_requires: International NGOs/foundations rely on GLs with recordkeeping.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Screening scope exists; license determination does not.
complexity_challenge: Default deny; counsel-approved GL citation unlocks.
analogy_breaks_down: Bank sanctions programs can reject even licensed transfers.
evidence: https://govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2022-12-21/html/2022-27639.htm (humanitarian/NGO general licenses across programs, 87 FR 78484; search-result summary, text not read) (accessed 2026-11-23)

industry: Nonprofit administration and grantmaking (private/community foundation practice)
capability: Excise-tax incident handling (taxable distribution, §4967 benefit, §4958 excess benefit)
business_problem: Detected violations need correction, return filing and board reporting.
why_industry_requires: PFs self-correct under §4945/§4941 and file Form 4720; public charities report excess benefits on Schedule L.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Same filings; no requirement exists.
complexity_challenge: One incident case type reusing the work queue.
analogy_breaks_down: None material.

industry: Government: tax administration / benefits administration / regulatory technology
capability: Information-return matching (IRS AUR-style payer/payee reconciliation)
