analogy_breaks_down: Government has subpoena-backed third-party data; sponsor has only its own ledger and public files.

industry: Government: tax administration / benefits administration / regulatory technology
capability: Ex parte eligibility redetermination (renew from trusted data before contacting the beneficiary)
business_problem: Reduce burden and churn at renewal.
why_industry_requires: Medicaid renewals use available data first (42 CFR 435.916 — unverified, general knowledge).
daf_equivalent_explanation: Charity re-verification from IRS/state data without contacting the charity.
complexity_challenge: Already the decision record's design (CA-180-06/09).
analogy_breaks_down: Charity is not an applicant with due-process rights; sponsor may deny for policy.

industry: Government: tax administration / benefits administration / regulatory technology
capability: Change-reporting duty and periodic redetermination
business_problem: Beneficiaries must report changes between renewals.
why_industry_requires: Benefits programs impose change reporting.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Only ER grantees have reporting duties; others are monitored by sponsor from public data.
complexity_challenge: Do not impose change-reporting on routine grantees.
analogy_breaks_down: Benefits recipients are obliged by law; charities owe sponsor nothing absent agreement.

industry: Government: tax administration / benefits administration / regulatory technology
capability: Adverse-action notice and fair hearing
business_problem: Due process before benefit termination.
why_industry_requires: Goldberg v. Kelly line (unverified detail).

complexity_challenge: Keep lightweight.

industry: Government: tax administration / benefits administration / regulatory technology
capability: Pre-payment integrity checks (Do Not Pay-style)

capability: Overpayment recovery

capability: Custody/titling of disbursement funds (no vendor-held float)
business_problem: If a for-profit vendor holds or moves charitable money, money-transmission and insolvency risk follow.
why_industry_requires: Payment facilitators segregate client money; failures (Flipcause, SDG Impact Fund) show commingling risk.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Not specified anywhere in Unbound.

capability: Operator regulatory-status register gated by feature activation (MT, IA, BD, GLBA FI, solicitation platform)
business_problem: Features silently change the operator's legal status.
why_industry_requires: Fintechs maintain licensing matrices per product.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-064 assigns roles; no gate ties features to status analyses.
complexity_challenge: Gate only the few features that change status.
analogy_breaks_down: Sponsor exclusions (Philanthropy Protection Act) do not extend to a for-profit vendor.

capability: Communications legal classification (CAN-SPAM commercial vs transactional; TCPA consent and revocation)
business_problem: Messages need correct consent/opt-out handling.
why_industry_requires: Marketers classify messages.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Notification catalog has consent basis but no legal class or revocation SLA.
complexity_challenge: Classify once per event type.
analogy_breaks_down: Nonprofit exemptions cover DNC rules, not autodialed texts.

capability: Accessibility (ADA/WCAG) obligations
business_problem: Accessible donor/charity UI.
why_industry_requires: Industry practice WCAG 2.x AA.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-GRANT-032 targets WCAG 2.2 AA; legal basis is case law/industry practice, not a Title III regulation.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: DOJ's 2024 Title II rule binds state/local governments, not private sponsors (general knowledge).

capability: Electronic signature of grant agreements with organizations
business_problem: Sign ER/conditional agreements electronically.
why_industry_requires: Universal.
daf_equivalent_explanation: E-SIGN consumer-consent (§7001(c)) does not apply to organization grantees (general knowledge).
complexity_challenge: Do not apply consumer disclosures to grantees.
analogy_breaks_down: Donor CWAs are consumer-facing; grantee agreements are B2B.

capability: Regulatory-change watch including temporary-regulation sunsets
business_problem: Rules expire or finalize.
why_industry_requires: Compliance teams track.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-RCN-REG-001 covers watch list; add §1.530A-7T expiry and NPRM.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: None.

capability: Typed tenant model (tenant vs legal sponsor vs distribution partner vs program vs deployment cell)
business_problem: Isolation key, ledger partition and policy scope use different words in different documents, so a leak or mis-partition is undetectable by review.
why_industry_requires: Multi-tenant SaaS defines one tenancy unit and binds every record, credential and cost to it.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-TEN-020 separates the dimensions and UNB-RCN-PLT-001 proposes the typed entities, but RCD-004 (what the tenant is) is still open.
complexity_challenge: Do not add a fifth dimension; close RCD-004 (tenant = legal sponsor recommended) and express partner/program as attributes inside the sponsor tenant.
automation_rationale: Tenancy is a type-system and routing fact; no judgement involved.
automation_risks: None if typed; risk is human mis-declaration at provisioning.
validation_evidence_needed: Isolation map per data class reviewed and enforced by a compile-time or CI check.
analogy_breaks_down: Ordinary SaaS tenant = paying customer; here the paying customer (partner) may not be the legal owner (sponsor), so billing tenant and legal tenant can differ.

capability: Isolation profiles (schema, database, dedicated cell) selected per tenant without code fork
business_problem: Institutional buyers demand stronger isolation; supporting every profile from day one multiplies tests and migrations.
why_industry_requires: Enterprise SaaS sells silo/pool/bridge tenancy tiers and must keep one codebase.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-TEN-002, UNB-PLAT-008 and RR-UNB-PLAT-008-r1 define the profiles; RCC-ARC-001 records the contradiction with one-system deployment.
complexity_challenge: None of the ten operating models inherently requires Profile C (see business-models.jsonl); keep one default and activate others only on cited contract clause.
automation_rationale: Profile is a deployment binding selected by an approved TenantIsolationDecision.
automation_risks: Profile drift between declared and actual infrastructure.
validation_evidence_needed: UNB-TEN-018 benchmark; per-profile isolation test suite; inventory reconciliation of declared vs deployed profile.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS tiers are priced options; here isolation can also be a legal-entity separation requirement between sponsors, so 'pool all sponsors in one schema' is not a pure price choice.

capability: White labeling (one Brand Kit across portal, widget, email, print, IVR)
business_problem: Each sponsor or partner wants its own brand without the platform forking UI or documents.
why_industry_requires: White-label SaaS must let resellers present their brand while the vendor keeps one product.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-030 Brand Kit; UNB-RCN-PLT-007 protected terms.
complexity_challenge: Brand is data (tokens, assets, terms); prohibit per-tenant templates that carry logic (REQ-X-057 'no template-defined financial logic').
automation_risks: Brand contrast failing WCAG; brand implying wrong legal sponsor.
validation_evidence_needed: Accessibility contrast check at publication; legal-sponsor disclosure present in every channel snapshot.
analogy_breaks_down: In consumer white label the reseller is the seller of record; in DAF white label the legal sponsor must still be disclosed as owner (LOM:13), so branding can never hide the sponsor.

capability: Custom terminology with protected legal terms
business_problem: Sponsors rename 'grant' or 'fund'; renaming must not change legal meaning of acknowledgments or affirmations.
why_industry_requires: SaaS localization/terminology layers let customers rename objects.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-RCN-ARC-002 terminology resolver and UNB-RCN-PLT-007 protected-term registry.
complexity_challenge: Keep one resolver; do not let email/IVR/AI each implement aliases.
automation_risks: AI assistant paraphrasing a protected term.
validation_evidence_needed: Golden tests of protected phrases across channels.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS renames are cosmetic; DAF terms like 'exclusive legal control' carry tax consequence.

capability: Versioned tenant configuration with lifecycle (draft, simulate, approve, schedule, activate, supersede)
business_problem: Configuration changes alter fees, minimums and approvals; untracked changes break audit and in-flight work.
why_industry_requires: Configuration-as-data with promotion and rollback is standard in regulated SaaS.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-045 and the sponsor configuration lifecycle.
complexity_challenge: Lifecycle has 8 states; acceptable because it mirrors policy approval. Do not add a separate config-promotion pipeline: sandbox-to-production promotion is a hash-equal re-approval.
automation_rationale: Validation and simulation deterministic; AI may explain diffs; approval human.
validation_evidence_needed: Simulation replay of last N months against proposed config.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS config rollback is instant; here rollback cannot rewrite as-issued decisions (SCP:14).

capability: Tenant-specific business rules as declarative policy, never tenant code
business_problem: Sponsors differ in minimums, approval thresholds, eligible charities; custom code per tenant fragments the product.
why_industry_requires: Multi-tenant SaaS avoids per-tenant code to keep one release.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-045 typed policy composition; REQ-X-057 prohibits sponsor forks.
complexity_challenge: Reject tenant scripting (XRJ-SAS-001).
automation_risks: Policy space grows until it is a programming language.
validation_evidence_needed: Catalog of all policy parameters with owner and test; count of parameters per release.
analogy_breaks_down: Platforms like CRM allow customer code; DAF sponsor legal authority makes executable tenant code an audit liability.

capability: Feature entitlements (contracted capability set per tenant/program)
business_problem: What a sponsor or partner has bought (e.g. complex assets, international grants, API access, AI assistance) is not represented; sales promises leak into policy or flags.
why_industry_requires: SaaS separates entitlement (what the contract allows) from configuration (how it is used) and feature flags (release mechanics).
daf_equivalent_explanation: No requirement models entitlements; REQ-X-045 mixes contract scope with sponsor policy.
complexity_challenge: One entitlement register keyed by tenant/program, consulted by authorization; no separate entitlement service.
validation_evidence_needed: Tests that removing an entitlement never cancels accepted grants or blocks statements/holds.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS can switch off a feature on non-payment; a DAF platform cannot switch off sponsor fiduciary functions (statements, holds, retention) on a commercial dispute.

capability: Feature flags (release toggles) with expiry and no semantic effect
business_problem: Shipping one release to all cells needs dark launch and kill switches; unmanaged flags become hidden tenant forks.
why_industry_requires: Continuous-delivery SaaS uses short-lived flags with ownership and expiry.
daf_equivalent_explanation: No flag requirement exists (inventory has zero 'feature flag' hits).
complexity_challenge: Cap flag lifetime; flags must not vary financial/legal semantics per tenant.
automation_rationale: Flag evaluation is deterministic and recorded.
automation_risks: Flag state not captured, breaking deterministic replay.
validation_evidence_needed: Replay equality test with recorded flag snapshot; stale-flag report.
analogy_breaks_down: Consumer SaaS uses flags for A/B experiments; experiments on legal notices or approvals are inappropriate here.

capability: Release management: one release train, ring-based rollout across cells, expand/contract schema migration
business_problem: Several cells and isolation profiles must upgrade without per-tenant code versions and without a migration failing half the fleet.
why_industry_requires: SaaS vendors run ring/canary deployments and backward-compatible schema changes.
daf_equivalent_explanation: RR-REQ-X-057-r1 requires identical release; SOC2-011 change management; UNB-WF-022 canary for policy; nothing defines ring order, halt criteria or schema fan-out (Strata has no schema templating per report 13).
complexity_challenge: Ring rollout is simpler than tenant-pinned versions; do not offer per-tenant version pinning (XRJ-SAS-004).
automation_rationale: Automated promotion gates on health metrics.
validation_evidence_needed: Rollout drill across >=3 cells with an injected failing migration.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS can roll forward fast; financial cells need a change freeze around period close and the December giving peak.

capability: Public vs private API tiers with deprecation windows
business_problem: Partners integrate against APIs; unannounced breaking changes break donor flows at partner sites.
why_industry_requires: API-first SaaS publishes versioned public APIs with deprecation policy and sunset headers.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-API-STD-003 names 'deprecation policy' without windows; UNB-RCN-ARC-001 sets the contract source of truth.
complexity_challenge: Three tiers suffice: internal (in-process), partner (contracted), public (published).
automation_rationale: CI breaking-change detection from generated schemas.
automation_risks: Classification of a change as non-breaking when semantics change.
validation_evidence_needed: Contract-diff CI with semantic annotations; consumer registry.
analogy_breaks_down: Public SaaS APIs can sunset with notice; partner APIs in a DAF carry in-flight grant recommendations that must still resolve.

capability: Webhooks and event subscriptions with subscription lifecycle, replay and minimization
business_problem: Partners and charities need status callbacks; without subscription governance data keeps flowing after offboarding and payloads overshare.
why_industry_requires: SaaS platforms run signed webhooks with retries, dead-letter, replay and per-subscriber scopes.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-API-006 and UNB-API-STD-005 require signing/replay defense; TVS-411 shows subscriptions surviving termination; no subscription lifecycle, delivery SLO or replay window.
complexity_challenge: Thin notifications (event type + resource id, fetch with auth) remove most payload-minimization work.
automation_risks: Retry storms; subscriber treating webhook as proof of settlement.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS webhooks are informational; a DAF 'grant paid' webhook may be treated by a charity as proof of funds, so status semantics must be exact (EXT:12).

capability: Tenant identity on every event, log and metric; prohibition of cross-tenant correlation
business_problem: Event streams, outboxes and telemetry are the commonest cross-tenant leak path and the input to tenant migration.
why_industry_requires: Multi-tenant SaaS stamps tenant context on every message and trace and denies cross-tenant joins.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-TEN-003/009 require isolation of streams/logs; UNB-DATA-002 requires correlation IDs; nothing mandates the envelope field or forbids a correlation/causation chain spanning tenants.
complexity_challenge: One envelope type shared by events, outbox and telemetry.
automation_risks: Global correlation id leaks sponsor relationships via telemetry vendor.
validation_evidence_needed: Property test: no event persisted without TenantId; no causation edge across TenantId except declared inter-cell contracts.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS tenant tagging is for billing; here it also defends sponsor confidentiality and §4966 legal-control separation.

capability: Embedded widgets in partner/host sites
business_problem: Advisor and nonprofit sites embed DAF functions; host must not gain authority or display false balances.
why_industry_requires: Embedded SaaS components (payments, scheduling) run scoped tokens and origin checks.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-063, INT-015, ADM-037, WG-1..WG-9, UNB-RCN-GRT-012.
complexity_challenge: Already over-specified (RCF-PLT-047 duplicate x5); consolidate.
validation_evidence_needed: Combined host+widget accessibility and overlay tests.
analogy_breaks_down: Payment widgets settle instantly; DAF widget outcome is a recommendation, not a payment (EXT:18).

capability: Integration catalog / third-party application registration with sponsor consent
business_problem: CRMs, wealth platforms and charity tools want API access; without registration, scopes and sponsor consent each integration is bespoke.
why_industry_requires: SaaS marketplaces register apps with OAuth scopes, review and tenant-admin consent.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-CUST-018 integration registry covers providers, not third-party apps acting for sponsors/donors.
complexity_challenge: Registry + consent only; no storefront or revenue share (XRJ-SAS-002).
automation_risks: App granted broader scope than sponsor intended.
validation_evidence_needed: Negative tests: unregistered client denied; consent revocation propagates.
analogy_breaks_down: App stores monetize; here every app touching donor data needs sponsor authority, so consent is per sponsor, not per user only.

capability: Data isolation across caches, queues, indexes, embeddings, backups, prompts
business_problem: Isolation enforced only in SQL leaks through search indexes, AI context and logs.
why_industry_requires: SaaS security programs extend tenancy to every store.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-TEN-009 and UNB-RCN-PLT-004.
complexity_challenge: None.
validation_evidence_needed: Store inventory reconciled to tenant-isolation test matrix.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Data migration into the platform (legacy import, parallel run, cutover)
business_problem: Institutions arrive with years of history on another vendor.
why_industry_requires: SaaS onboarding includes data conversion tooling.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-061 and RR-REQ-X-061-r1 MigrationRun state machine.
complexity_challenge: Covered; missing only the donor-facing transition window (UNB-XIN-OTH-002).
automation_rationale: Mapping AI-assisted, reconciliation deterministic, cutover human.
validation_evidence_needed: Tie-out by fund/position/period; synthetic legacy fixtures.
analogy_breaks_down: Ordinary SaaS conversions can drop history; DAF needs as-issued document provenance and tax-relevant history.

capability: Tenant onboarding/provisioning lifecycle with readiness gates
business_problem: Sponsor launch spans contract, board delegation, SSO, config, custody, payments; activation by brand publication alone is unsafe.
why_industry_requires: SaaS provisioning is automated with readiness checklists.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-TEN-011 requires a governed plan; REQ-X-064/REQ-X-071 list lifecycle phases; no explicit tenant state machine with gates.
complexity_challenge: Use one TenantLifecycle state machine for onboarding, suspension and exit (RR-UNB-TEN-011-r1).
automation_risks: Tenant goes Live with missing board delegation evidence.
validation_evidence_needed: Gate test: activation blocked without each gate evidence.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS self-serve signup is minutes; a sponsor tenant cannot go live without legal-entity evidence.

capability: Sponsor (legal entity) exit from the platform with export, read-only continuity and verified destruction
business_problem: A sponsor leaving must keep its records, satisfy retention, and get destruction evidence; append-only stores complicate deletion.
why_industry_requires: SaaS exit clauses give data export and certified deletion.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-TEN-016, REQ-X-061 and RCC-ENT-005 resolution (tenant-scoped chains, per-tenant key destruction) exist but are not written into one testable requirement.
complexity_challenge: Crypto-shred per tenant key instead of row deletion.
automation_rationale: Export and verification deterministic; destruction authorization human.
automation_risks: Destruction while a legal hold exists.
validation_evidence_needed: Exit drill with a seeded hold.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS deletion is the default; here statutory retention often outlives the contract and belongs to the sponsor.

capability: Distribution-partner exit with fund portability to a new sponsor
business_problem: A wealth firm or program leaving one sponsor for another wants its donors' funds to follow; funds are the old sponsor's property.
why_industry_requires: SaaS customers take their data; here the 'customer' (partner) does not own the assets.
daf_equivalent_explanation: RR-UNB-WF-014-r1 covers one donor-recommended transfer; nothing covers a program-level exit with thousands of funds, consent capture, non-consenting donors and partner-federated credentials (TVF-135).
complexity_challenge: Treat as a batch of ordinary outbound transfer grants; do not create a 'program migration' that moves ownership by data operation.
automation_rationale: Batch preparation deterministic; each transfer is a sponsor decision (may be policy-approved).
automation_risks: Bulk transfer executed as data reassignment, bypassing sponsor discretion.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel opinion on program transfer; drill with consenting, silent and objecting donors.
analogy_breaks_down: HSA/IRA trustee-to-trustee transfers are owner-directed rights; a DAF donor has only advisory privileges, so the old sponsor may decline.

capability: API documentation generated from authoritative contracts
business_problem: Hand-written docs drift from behaviour.
why_industry_requires: API-first SaaS generates reference docs from specs.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-API-STD-006 and UNB-RCN-ARC-001.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: AI-readable component and configuration documentation
business_problem: AI assistants guess at semantics without machine-readable contracts.
why_industry_requires: Developer platforms now publish machine-readable tool/contract manifests.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-051, RR-REQ-X-051-r1, AIC contracts.
complexity_challenge: Generate structural parts; keep editorial annotations small (AIC:33).
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Tenant-visible audit log including platform-operator access
business_problem: Sponsors cannot see when vendor staff touched their data.
why_industry_requires: Enterprise SaaS offers customer-facing access transparency logs.
daf_equivalent_explanation: SOC2-002/025 and MON-016 give evidence and auditor access; TVF-134 asks that sponsors receive operator access logs, not adopted.
complexity_challenge: Project the existing audit stream filtered by tenant; no second log.
validation_evidence_needed: Sponsor-side query test of operator access within N minutes.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS transparency is a feature; here sponsor exclusive legal control makes unreviewed operator access a governance defect.

capability: Security monitoring with tenant attribution
business_problem: Alerts without tenant context cannot be routed to the affected sponsor or assessed for notification duties.
why_industry_requires: SaaS SOCs correlate by tenant for breach notification.
daf_equivalent_explanation: SOC2-012 and SOC2-027 define scope; MON-013 tenant isolation of monitoring.
complexity_challenge: Use the envelope from UNB-XIN-SAS-005; no separate tagging.
validation_evidence_needed: Detection test library per tenant profile.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Disaster recovery objectives by data class
business_problem: Per-capability RPO/RTO cannot be tested; a ledger and a search index need different objectives.
why_industry_requires: SaaS publishes RPO/RTO by service tier and data class.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-006 sets RPO zero for acknowledged authoritative commits; UNB-RES-003 per capability; UNB-TEN-014 tenant restore caveats; no class table.
complexity_challenge: One table of ~7 classes replaces per-capability objectives.
validation_evidence_needed: Annual restore drill per class and per isolation profile.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS can accept seconds of loss for most data; acknowledged financial commits cannot.

capability: Observability (traces, metrics, logs) with tenant attribution and telemetry isolation
business_problem: Operators need per-tenant health; telemetry vendors receive identifiers that can leak.
why_industry_requires: SaaS observability is tenant-tagged with PII scrubbing.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-TEN-009 lists observability; SOC2-003 privacy-aware logging.
complexity_challenge: Covered by envelope (SAS-005) plus metering (SAS-009).
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Availability SLOs and error budgets
business_problem: Without SLOs there is no objective basis for release freezes, partner SLAs or service credits.
why_industry_requires: SRE practice: SLIs per user journey, SLO targets, error-budget policy that halts releases.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADM-033 SLAs, UNB-TEN-015 per-partner targets and REQ-X-071 service catalog; none defines SLIs, budgets or release consequences.
complexity_challenge: Budget availability/latency only; never budget financial correctness (zero tolerance).
automation_risks: Gaming SLIs by excluding Unknown outcomes.
validation_evidence_needed: SLI definitions reviewed; burn-rate alert tests.
analogy_breaks_down: Web SRE budgets errors; a duplicated payment is not an 'error' to budget.
evidence: https://sre.google/workbook/error-budget-policy/ (accessed 2026-11-23; search-result excerpt: example error budget policy halts releases when budget exhausted)

capability: Per-tenant metering and cost attribution (storage, compute, API, AI, provider calls)
business_problem: Cost-to-serve per sponsor/program/model is unknowable, so pricing, isolation-tier economics (ADR-009) and the high-volume-low-balance model cannot be evaluated.
why_industry_requires: SaaS meters usage per tenant for pricing and capacity.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-071 asks for cost-to-serve, UNB-RCN-PLT-006 measures human touches; nothing meters resource use.
complexity_challenge: Meter from the same envelope; allocate shared costs by declared keys monthly; no real-time billing engine.
automation_risks: Metering used as an authorization input.
validation_evidence_needed: Reconciliation of metered totals to cloud invoice within tolerance.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS bills by usage; DAF fees are charitable-asset fees governed by sponsor policy (REQ-X-067), so metering informs pricing, never fund-level fee accrual directly.

capability: Sandbox tenants with synthetic data and no live rails
business_problem: Sponsors and partners must test config and integrations without touching production data or money.
why_industry_requires: SaaS provides sandbox orgs.
daf_equivalent_explanation: SCP:17 mentions sponsor sandbox; UNB-CUST-024 provider sandboxes; nothing forbids production data copy or live-rail reach.
complexity_challenge: Sandbox = a normal tenant with environment class Sandbox; no separate stack.
validation_evidence_needed: Network-level proof sandbox cannot resolve live rail endpoints.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS sandboxes often clone production; here cloning donor PII into sandbox is a privacy breach.

capability: Tenant quotas, rate limits and noisy-neighbour control
business_problem: One partner's batch or December surge degrades others.
why_industry_requires: Pooled SaaS enforces per-tenant fair share.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-TEN-015 and UNB-API-STD-003.
complexity_challenge: None.
validation_evidence_needed: Surge test with priority classes (holds never throttled).
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Subprocessor register and tenant notification of changes
business_problem: Sponsors' DPAs and SOC CUEC reviews need to know which vendors process their donors' data.
why_industry_requires: SaaS DPAs commit to subprocessor lists and advance notice.
daf_equivalent_explanation: SOC2-013 vendor inventory; UNB-TEN-008 per-partner DPA; GAP-016 subprocessor assurance; no notice obligation.
complexity_challenge: Publish register from vendor inventory; notice by template email.
analogy_breaks_down: Same practice; DAF sponsors are often less sophisticated buyers than enterprise SaaS customers.

capability: Per-tenant incident and status communication
business_problem: During incidents sponsors must know impact to their donors and grants to discharge their own duties.
why_industry_requires: SaaS status pages and per-customer incident notices.
daf_equivalent_explanation: SOC2-026 incident communication; REQ-X-071 sponsor communication via work queue.
complexity_challenge: Use notification catalog (UNB-RCN-PLT-002) with an incident class; no separate status product.
automation_rationale: Impact scoping deterministic from envelope; wording human.
validation_evidence_needed: Incident drill measuring time-to-notify per tenant.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Separate identity realms for platform workforce, sponsor workforce and customers (donors, advisors, charities, partner users)
business_problem: One identity store for all actors lets a donor credential reach staff functions and makes partner exit a mass-recovery event.
why_industry_requires: Enterprise SaaS separates workforce IAM from CIAM, with federated enterprise SSO per customer.
daf_equivalent_explanation: CTL-033 distinguishes workforce MFA from donor step-up; SOC2-010 covers workforce access; AUTH-I8 fixes partner mapping keys; no realm separation requirement.
complexity_challenge: Three realms, one authorization model (REQ-X-057 'one identity framework' kept).
automation_rationale: Realm is fixed at principal creation.
automation_risks: Same human holding staff and donor roles merges privileges.
validation_evidence_needed: Negative test: donor-realm token rejected at staff endpoints; realm-crossing link audited.
analogy_breaks_down: CIAM in retail is about conversion; here customer identities exercise advisory privileges over charitable assets.

capability: Per-tenant enterprise SSO federation and SCIM lifecycle
business_problem: Sponsor and partner staff come from their own IdPs; leavers must lose access.
why_industry_requires: B2B SaaS federates per tenant and deprovisions via SCIM.
daf_equivalent_explanation: CTL-052, AUTH-I8, TVS-407, TVS-415.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Step-up authentication matrix by action class with freshness bound to the command
business_problem: Session-level MFA does not protect payee changes, authority changes, exports or large grants.
why_industry_requires: Banking and SaaS admin consoles require re-authentication for sensitive actions (NIST AAL, reauthentication).
daf_equivalent_explanation: CTL-033 and AUTH-I7 require step-up for payout-relevant/authority changes; TVF-136 shows partner-held confirmation gap; no matrix with AAL and max age.
complexity_challenge: One table; do not let each workflow define its own.
automation_risks: Step-up fatigue causing helpdesk recovery abuse.
analogy_breaks_down: Banks own the money; DAF donors only recommend, so step-up protects recommendation integrity and sponsor payee data rather than donor balances.
evidence: https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b/aal (accessed 2026-11-23; search-result excerpt: AAL2 must offer phishing-resistant option; reauthentication timeout)

capability: Delegated and agent principals (on-behalf-of, expiry, parent-derived)
business_problem: Advisors, assistants and AI agents act for donors or staff; revocation must cascade.
why_industry_requires: OAuth token exchange/on-behalf-of and workload identities in SaaS.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-API-003, SOC2-017, GOV-AUTH-003/015, AUTH-I1/I2, UNB-RCN-PLT-004/005.
complexity_challenge: None; avoid a separate agent IAM.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Platform-operator (vendor workforce) access to tenant data under sponsor authority
business_problem: Under outsourced/infrastructure models operator staff are not covered by the sponsor's delegation of authority.
why_industry_requires: Enterprise SaaS 'customer lockbox' patterns require customer approval for support access.
daf_equivalent_explanation: TVF-134 states the requirement as a finding; TVS-421 scenario; CTL-031 JIT without sponsor approver.
complexity_challenge: Pre-approved DoA categories plus per-case approval for anything else.
validation_evidence_needed: Test operator write attempt without sponsor DoA.
analogy_breaks_down: Cloud lockbox protects confidentiality; here it also protects the sponsor's exclusive legal control over charitable assets.

capability: Access reviews / recertification with auto-revocation
business_problem: Stale privileges accumulate across sponsors, partners, banks and custodians.
why_industry_requires: SOX/SOC2 user access reviews.
daf_equivalent_explanation: GOV-AUTH-025, SOC2-010, SOC-T07, AUTH-I6 require reviews; no cadence, reviewer independence or auto-revoke.
complexity_challenge: Risk-tiered cadence; auto-revoke unreviewed.
automation_rationale: Population and diff deterministic; AI can flag anomalies; attestation human.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Break-glass emergency access
business_problem: Responders need access when IdP or command service is down, without creating an unaudited path to authority/payee changes.
why_industry_requires: SaaS keeps sealed emergency accounts with alerting.
daf_equivalent_explanation: TVS-441, TVS-473, TVF-139, TVF-228 identify the gap; CTL-031 JIT; no adopted requirement.
complexity_challenge: Break-glass may only freeze, hold and read; never perform domain transitions.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Sponsor-direct credential for partner-federated donors
business_problem: Donors who only log in via a partner IdP lose access at partner exit.
why_industry_requires: SaaS with B2B2C federation keeps a fallback direct credential.
daf_equivalent_explanation: TVF-135/TVS-409; covered for exit by UNB-XIN-SAS-007 AC.
complexity_challenge: Pre-register a sponsor-direct factor at first login.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Authority and session revocation propagation with stated maximum staleness
business_problem: Revoked advisors keep seeing data in open widgets.
why_industry_requires: SaaS session revocation SLAs.
daf_equivalent_explanation: AUTH-I1, WG-1.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Retention schedule (class catalog with authority, trigger, period)
business_problem: Records kept too briefly breach law; kept forever increase breach exposure.
why_industry_requires: Records management assigns each record a schedule class (ISO 15489 practice).
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-037, RR-REQ-X-036-r1 with OFAC 10y etc.; counsel approval pending (RCD-007).
complexity_challenge: Class-level, not per-record decisions.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Legal holds with custodian notice, processor propagation and survival across migration/exit
business_problem: Holds that stop at the platform boundary let partners, print vendors or the old cell destroy evidence.
why_industry_requires: Litigation hold practice: documented trigger, notice to custodians and third parties, monitoring, timely release.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-038 covers in-platform matching/serialization; TVS-484 shows partner deletion under subpoena; nothing propagates holds to processors, partners or migration targets.
complexity_challenge: Hold record carries scope; propagation is an outbox effect to each registered processor.
automation_risks: AI deciding a hold is unnecessary.
validation_evidence_needed: Hold drill across a migration and a partner offboarding.
analogy_breaks_down: Corporate holds target employees as custodians; here custodians include external processors and other sponsors' cells.
evidence: https://www.thesedonaconference.org/sites/default/files/publications/Commentary%20on%20Legal%20Holds%20Second%20Edition%20extended%20PC%20period_0.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23; search-result summary; marked superseded, verify current edition)

capability: Defensible disposition by approved class-level batches
business_problem: Per-record human review at expiry does not scale and is not more defensible.
why_industry_requires: Defensible disposition = consistent application of an approved schedule with documented exceptions.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-038 independent approval per DispositionCase; RR-REQ-X-036-r1 'expiry MUST create a disposition review task'; RCD-007 recommends class-level batches; RCF-PLT-014.
complexity_challenge: One approval per class batch per period; re-check holds at execution.
automation_risks: Batch approved while a later hold lands.
validation_evidence_needed: Batch disposition drill with racing hold.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.
evidence: https://www.thesedonaconference.org/sites/default/files/publications/Commentary%20on%20Legal%20Holds%20Second%20Edition%20extended%20PC%20period_0.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23; search-result summary; marked superseded, verify current edition)

capability: eDiscovery / regulatory production with chain of custody
business_problem: A state AG subpoena or litigation needs a scoped, hashed, redaction-logged production per tenant.
why_industry_requires: Records/eDiscovery practice: collection, processing, production with chain of custody.
daf_equivalent_explanation: SOC2-009/MON-015 evidence packages are for auditors, not legal production.
complexity_challenge: Reuse Folio evidence package builder with a legal-production profile.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Erasure in append-only stores via per-subject/per-tenant key destruction
business_problem: Privacy requests and tenant exit conflict with immutable events.
why_industry_requires: Crypto-shredding is the standard pattern for immutable logs.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-DATA-007, UNB-IMM-008, RCC-ENT-005 resolution.
complexity_challenge: Per-tenant key at exit; per-subject vault for PII.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Records custodianship after sponsor exit
business_problem: Who keeps the seven-year financial records once the sponsor leaves the platform is undefined.
why_industry_requires: Outsourced recordkeeping contracts name the custodian of record.
daf_equivalent_explanation: RCC-PLT-008 defers to sponsor contract and counsel.
complexity_challenge: Default: sponsor is custodian; platform keeps only what its own obligations require.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Human task queues with routing and cradle-to-grave ownership
business_problem: Exceptions need owners.
why_industry_requires: Workflow suites provide work queues.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-048 and RR-REQ-X-048-r1.
complexity_challenge: WorkItems only on deterministic block (RR-REQ-X-048-r1).
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Durable timers, deadlines and obligations
business_problem: Form 8282 windows, stale checks, 180-day refresh, hold expiries, SLA clocks and cooling-off periods must fire exactly once even across restarts and restores.
why_industry_requires: Durable-execution engines (Temporal etc.) persist timers; BPMN engines have timer events.
daf_equivalent_explanation: TIME-1 defines calendars; ADM-033 SLAs; individual requirements state deadlines; no single persisted timer/obligation mechanism.
complexity_challenge: A timer table in the authoritative DB plus one scheduler is sufficient; no engine.
validation_evidence_needed: Restore drill: no timer fires twice or is lost.
analogy_breaks_down: Engines own workflow state; in Unbound the domain aggregate owns state and the timer is only a wake-up.

capability: Transactional outbox and external-effect orchestration
business_problem: External effects must not duplicate on retry.
why_industry_requires: Outbox/inbox pattern.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-EVT-002, REQ-X-020/021, UNB-DATA-009, REQ-X-083.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Long-running process instance version pinning and migration
business_problem: A grant or migration that started under definition v3 must not silently change rules when v4 ships.
why_industry_requires: BPMN/durable engines version workflow definitions per instance.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-045 pins policy versions to transactions; UNB-DATA-010 upcasters for events; nothing covers state-machine definition changes for in-flight instances.
complexity_challenge: Pin policy version + state-machine schema version at start; explicit migration command for in-flight.
analogy_breaks_down: Engines replay code (determinism constraints); Unbound replays events, so code changes need upcasters, not workflow-history replay.

capability: Visual (BPMN) process authoring by sponsors
business_problem: Sponsors want to change approval steps.
why_industry_requires: BPM suites let analysts draw processes.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-045 deliberately uses declarative policy parameters instead.
complexity_challenge: Rejected (XRJ-WFA-002): parameters + routing policy cover the variation.
analogy_breaks_down: BPM processes are owned by the enterprise; DAF process steps include statutory gates the sponsor may not remove.

capability: Compensation for multi-step processes
business_problem: Partial completion needs governed reversal.
why_industry_requires: Saga compensation.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-API-STD-002, REQ-X-083, UNB-IMM-003.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Durable-workflow engine runtime (Temporal/Camunda class)
business_problem: Considered for timers, retries and long-running state.
why_industry_requires: Used widely for orchestration.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Not required; in-DB state machines + outbox + timer table cover the need (see REPORT).
complexity_challenge: Rejected for release 1 (XRJ-WFA-001; XID-WFA-001).
automation_risks: Second durable store and determinism constraints.
analogy_breaks_down: Engine owns state; Unbound requires the ledger/aggregates to own authoritative state in one transaction.

capability: Trustee / program manager / recordkeeper / distributor role split with named disclosure
business_problem: Clients cannot tell who owns, administers and distributes the account.
why_industry_requires: State trust is the plan sponsor; a program manager administers under contract; recordkeeper books transactions; a primary distributor underwrites.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-064 SponsorOperatingAgreement binds sponsor, administrator, vendor, distributor; LOM:13 disclosure.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: 529 owner owns the account and can roll it over; DAF donor has advisory privileges only. 529 is a municipal-securities regime (MSRB); DAFs are not securities offerings.
evidence: https://www.sec.gov/comments/sr-msrb-2013-04/msrb201304-11.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23; search-result summary of MSRB comment letter, not full read)

capability: Standardized machine-readable program description (fees, investment options, roles) per program (MSRB Form G-45 analog)
business_problem: Advisors and donors compare programs by marketing pages; fees and options per white-label program are opaque.
why_industry_requires: Underwriters report plan descriptive info, fees and investment options to the MSRB.
daf_equivalent_explanation: No requirement publishes a per-program disclosure data set; REQ-X-067 and UNB-RCN-FIN-005 define fees internally.
complexity_challenge: Generate from existing fee/option configuration; no new data entry.
analogy_breaks_down: G-45 is mandatory regulatory reporting; for DAFs this is voluntary transparency, so P3.
evidence: https://www.sec.gov/comments/sr-msrb-2013-04/msrb201304-11.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23; search-result summary of MSRB comment letter, not full read)

capability: Program-specific investment option lineup with age/target or static portfolios
business_problem: Each white-label program offers different options.
why_industry_requires: 529 and HSA platforms offer per-plan lineups.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-INV/NAV families and RCD-017; DAF pools are sponsor-owned.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Age-based glide paths have no DAF equivalent (no beneficiary age); spend-down horizon (UNB-HYP-009) is the nearest.

capability: Custodian vs administrator split, white-label via banks, trustee-to-trustee transfers
business_problem: Banks and benefits platforms brand HSAs on a nonbank trustee's platform; accounts move between custodians on owner request.
why_industry_requires: Only banks, insurers or IRS-approved nonbank trustees may hold HSA assets; administrators and white-label distributors sit on top.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Role split maps to REQ-X-064; transfer maps to RR-UNB-WF-014-r1 but DAF transfers are sponsor-discretionary.
complexity_challenge: None.
automation_risks: Treating DAF transfer as owner right.
analogy_breaks_down: HSA owner owns assets and has a statutory transfer right; DAF sponsor holds exclusive legal control. HSA is high-volume-low-balance with card spend; DAF grants are vetted.
evidence: https://www.irs.gov/node/3229 (accessed 2026-11-23; search-result summary: nonbank trustee approval via Rev. Proc. and Treas. Reg. 1.408-2(e))

capability: Agent authority register: authority granted per client, terminated by successor appointment, liability stays with principal
business_problem: Switching provider must cut off the old agent's authority cleanly.
why_industry_requires: IRS reporting-agent authorization: a new authorization terminates the prior agent; liability remains with the employer.
daf_equivalent_explanation: AUTH-I6 third-party authority registers; REQ-X-064 contract roles; partner exit (UNB-XIN-SAS-007) needs the same 'new appointment terminates old' rule for provider authorities.
complexity_challenge: Model provider authority as an effective-dated relationship with automatic supersession.
automation_risks: Two providers both believing they are authorized.
analogy_breaks_down: Payroll agents remit employer money on fixed statutory schedules; DAF providers act on sponsor discretion.
evidence: https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/reporting-agents-file-raf (accessed 2026-11-23; search-result summary: new reporting agent authorization terminates prior agent; Form 8655 does not transfer liability)

capability: High-volume year-end document production (W-2 analog: annual donor summaries, contribution acknowledgments) with corrections
business_problem: January peak of statutory documents across all clients.
why_industry_requires: Payroll firms batch-produce, file and correct year-end forms.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-032 statements, REQ-X-034 artifact registry, UNB-RCN-FIN-001 acknowledgments.
complexity_challenge: Reuse statement pipeline; capacity test January.
analogy_breaks_down: Payroll forms are filed with the IRS; DAF acknowledgments go only to donors (sponsor files Schedule D).

capability: Recordkeeper conversion with participant transition window (blackout) notice
business_problem: Moving recordkeepers freezes some transactions; participants must know in advance what they cannot do and for how long.
why_industry_requires: Plan conversions use a published blackout period with advance participant notice (ERISA blackout notice rules).
daf_equivalent_explanation: RR-REQ-X-061-r1 defines migration states but no donor-/charity-facing transition window with frozen-action list.
complexity_challenge: Derive frozen-action list from the cutover plan automatically.
analogy_breaks_down: ERISA notice is legally required; for DAFs it is a customer obligation/contract matter; DAF grants to charities may be time-sensitive (December).

capability: Conditional disbursement and out-of-band verification of wire instruction changes
business_problem: Wire-instruction fraud diverts closing funds.
why_industry_requires: Escrow releases funds only on documented conditions and verifies instruction changes by call-back to known numbers.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-005 destination integrity; UNB-RCN-GRT-017 DestinationEvidence; SCN-05.
complexity_challenge: None.
automation_rationale: Evidence check deterministic; call-back human or bank-verified.
automation_risks: Call-back to number supplied in the fraud email.
analogy_breaks_down: Escrow holds funds for two parties with conditions; DAF sponsor owns the funds outright.

capability: Intermediary never holds or routes funds; a qualified third party holds them
business_problem: Platforms that touch funds take on custody risk and regulation.
why_industry_requires: Funding portals must direct investor funds to a qualified third party and may not handle investor funds.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-063 forbids balance exposure and second grant engines but does not state that hosts/partners never receive or route funds; OB-38 CA platform law remittance duty.
complexity_challenge: One invariant on the funds-flow graph.
automation_risks: Partner settlement account inserted as intermediary payee.
analogy_breaks_down: Reg CF regulates securities offerings; DAF grants are not investments. The transferable idea is the structural separation of the intermediary from funds.
evidence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/17/227.303 (accessed 2026-11-23; search-result summary: funding portal must direct investor funds to a qualified third party; may not hold funds)

capability: Claimant verification, withholding and unclaimed-prize handling
business_problem: Large payouts to verified winners with tax withholding; unclaimed funds revert.
why_industry_requires: Lotteries verify claimants, withhold tax and handle expiry.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Unclaimed/stale checks map to UNB-RCN-GRT-005 and UNB-WF-015; claimant verification maps to charity verification REQ-X-007.
complexity_challenge: Nothing new; see XRJ-OTH-001.
analogy_breaks_down: Payees are individuals with withholding; DAF payees are charities, no withholding.

capability: Unitized pooled investment with fund-level restrictions and spending policy
business_problem: Many named funds share one pool with restrictions.
why_industry_requires: Endowments unitize pools and track donor restrictions (UPMIFA).
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-RCN-FIN-007 attribution method; NAV unitization; restrictions as balancing segments UNB-RCN-FIN-006.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Endowments are perpetual institutional funds with spending rules; DAF funds are spendable at donor recommendation subject to sponsor approval.

capability: Check print and mail chain of custody: print manifest reconciliation, Intelligent Mail barcode tracking, returned-mail handling
business_problem: Checks and statutory letters leave the platform through print vendors; without piece-level reconciliation a check can be printed twice, lost or mailed to a stale address.
why_industry_requires: Mail-order fulfillment and statement printers reconcile every piece (printed, spoiled, inserted, mailed) and use USPS IMb scans for visibility.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-RCN-GRT-005 check states, TVS-505 vendor timeout, REQ-X-083; no manifest reconciliation, IMb events or returned-mail rule.
complexity_challenge: Treat mail scans as evidence of transit only; positive pay remains the control.
validation_evidence_needed: Vendor contract test with spoil/reprint fixtures.
analogy_breaks_down: Parcel tracking proves delivery to an address; it does not prove the intended charity controlled the check or deposited it.
evidence: https://postalpro.usps.com/mnt/glusterfs/2024-05/FAQ_IV-MTR_API_v3.0_0.pdf (accessed 2026-11-23; search-result excerpt: IV-MTR piece scans, assumed/logical events, 30-day API data window)

capability: Electronic document delivery tracking (sent, bounced, opened/available, fallback to mail)
business_problem: Statutory notices undelivered by email must fall back.
why_industry_requires: Fulfillment tracks delivery and exceptions per item.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-DOC-004 receipts; REQ-X-028 as-sent history; UNB-RCN-PLT-002 notification catalog.
complexity_challenge: None.
analogy_breaks_down: Same.

capability: Customer and product cost-to-serve (activity costing of branch, contact, payment and servicing activities per account and product)
business_problem: Bank cannot see which accounts/products destroy value because servicing cost is buried in shared overhead.
why_industry_requires: Thin-margin fee and spread products need per-product and per-segment profitability to price and to rationalise service channels.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-043 names unit economics ("what does each transaction, fund, sponsor and exception actually cost") and lists economics KPIs but defines no attribution entities, methods or reconciliation.
complexity_challenge: Do not copy bank-style full absorption costing of every overhead line onto each fund; attribute direct and time-driven costs to cost objects and keep overhead in an explicit residual layer (CM3) instead of spreading it.
automation_rationale: Allocation is arithmetic over versioned rules and metered events; no judgement once rules are approved.
automation_risks: Rule errors silently mis-price segments; precision theatre on low-confidence allocations.
validation_evidence_needed: Shadow-replay measured unit times and vendor invoices for one sponsor month; reconcile to GL.
analogy_breaks_down: Banks earn net interest margin on balances; a DAF sponsor does not lend and fund assets are irrevocably contributed charitable assets, so balance-driven profit attribution does not transfer.

capability: Funds transfer pricing (FTP) of deposits and loans to split net interest margin across business lines
business_problem: Allocating interest-rate margin between deposit-gathering and lending units.
why_industry_requires: Banks intermediate maturity and liquidity; FTP is how they attribute NIM and rate risk.
daf_equivalent_explanation: DAF sponsors do not run a deposit/loan book. Fund assets are invested for the fund (pool/NAV) and cash income belongs to funds or the sponsor per policy (FI-36 owner/destination rule). There is no internal spread to transfer-price. The only near-analogue is interest on in-transit/float cash, which FI-36 already assigns an owner.
complexity_challenge: Reject FTP. Treat any float/in-transit interest as an explicitly owned income item (FI-36) and a RevenueRecord with source, never as a transfer price that credits operations for holding donor money.
automation_rationale: Owner/destination of float income is a sponsor policy setting, not a pricing model.
automation_risks: A synthetic "float credit" would create an incentive to delay grant payment, a donor-harm and possibly a private-benefit concern.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel/CPA confirmation of float-income ownership per sponsor model.
analogy_breaks_down: No maturity transformation, no lending, no deposit liability: the economic substrate of FTP is absent.

capability: Customer profitability "whale curve" (cumulative profit by customer showing a minority subsidising losses)
business_problem: Average margins hide that a minority of customers generate most profit and many are served at a loss.
why_industry_requires: Drives pricing, minimums, channel migration and service-tier design.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Daf-landscape shows cost per account rises with fund size at community foundations (elasticity 1.22), so per-account averages mislead; fee schedules have minimums (Fidelity $100, Ren/RCF $250). No platform view of margin by fund segment exists.
complexity_challenge: Profitability by donor must never influence compliance, approval or charity verification depth. Restrict to segment and service-model level for pricing decisions; individual-fund margin visible only to finance roles.
automation_rationale: Aggregation over attributed cost and revenue records.
automation_risks: Use of fund-level margin to deprioritise low-balance donors in queues (fairness and fiduciary concern).
validation_evidence_needed: Measured attributed cost by balance band for at least one sponsor; fee revenue by band from ledger.
analogy_breaks_down: Donors are not customers in the legal sense for charitable assets: fees are charged to sponsor-owned funds; "unprofitable" funds may be mission-intended (community foundations).

capability: Normalized cost and usage data schema (FOCUS) for multi-vendor technology spend including AI, SaaS and cloud
business_problem: Vendor invoices use incompatible schemas, so cost cannot be joined to usage or allocated consistently.
why_industry_requires: FinOps needs one schema for billed vs effective cost, charge category, period and allocation columns.
daf_equivalent_explanation: No Unbound requirement normalizes vendor cost lines (cloud, model API, charity data vendors, payment rail, custody, bank) into a common cost-record schema. UNB-KNOW-024 declares connector costs only for charity data sources.
complexity_challenge: Adopt a FOCUS-aligned subset (BilledCost, EffectiveCost, ChargeCategory, ChargePeriodStart/End, SubAccountId, Tags, AllocatedMethodId) rather than inventing a schema; ingest monthly invoices plus metered per-event usage where the vendor provides it.
automation_rationale: Schema mapping per vendor adapter; mapping changes are versioned.
automation_risks: Mapping drift when a vendor changes invoice format; unmapped lines must fall to residual, not be dropped.
validation_evidence_needed: Map three real vendor invoice formats (cloud, model API, payment processor) in mock mode.
analogy_breaks_down: FOCUS targets technology billing; labour, custody basis-point fees and bank analysis statements need extension columns (x_ prefix).

capability: Showback versus chargeback of shared costs to consuming teams/tenants
business_problem: Consumers cannot see the cost they cause; or charging them formally requires accounting-grade allocation.
why_industry_requires: FinOps Foundation treats showback as required and chargeback as optional, depending on accounting policy; shared costs may be held centrally or allocated by consumption.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-TEN-007 classifies shared services across partners; REQ-X-067 contracts fees. No rule says whether sponsor-level cost views are informational (showback) or drive invoices (chargeback).
complexity_challenge: Default to showback. Chargeback only where a sponsor contract prices on cost-plus or pass-through, and then only through UNB-ACC-010 fee/billing posting with approval, never directly from the attribution model.
automation_rationale: Per-contract choice; posting path already exists in accounting.
automation_risks: Allocated (grade C/D) costs invoiced as if precise; disputes.
validation_evidence_needed: Contract review of at least one pass-through institutional model.
analogy_breaks_down: Cloud teams are internal; sponsors are legally separate charities. Chargeback to a sponsor is a commercial invoice with contract and disclosure implications, not an internal transfer.

capability: Tagging / attribution keys at resource and event creation time
business_problem: Costs that are not tagged at source cannot be attributed later without guesswork.
why_industry_requires: FinOps attribution quality is bounded by tag coverage; untagged spend is reported as such.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-043 read models carry sponsor IDs, event IDs and effective/known-at timestamps, which are natural cost-object keys, but no requirement makes cost-object tagging of every billable activity and external call mandatory or measures coverage.
complexity_challenge: Reuse existing domain event envelope (sponsor, fund, grant, case, correlation id) as the attribution key; do not add a separate tagging system.
automation_rationale: Envelope fields are set by the domain command, not inferred.
automation_risks: Background jobs and batch provider calls lack a single cost object; must carry a batch id and an allocation rule.
validation_evidence_needed: Tag coverage metric on mock replay (share of external-call cost with a resolvable cost object).
analogy_breaks_down: Cloud tags are free text set by engineers; here the keys are typed domain identifiers, which is stronger.

capability: Unit economics per AI invocation and per agent run, with budgets, anomaly detection and pre-execution estimates
business_problem: AI spend scales with re-runs, context size and tool loops; cost is invisible until the invoice.
why_industry_requires: FinOps unit-economics practice ties spend to business units of value; LLM ops add token budgets.
daf_equivalent_explanation: AIN-028 bounds token/tool/time budgets; CTL-027 monitors cost and latency anomalies; economic-model §4 sets ~$4/dossier and ~$0.31/routine-run materiality. Missing: per-run cost attribution to the grant/case cost object and a pre-execution estimate.
complexity_challenge: Keep deterministic rules on refresh paths (TVR-ECON-002) so most AI cost is avoided rather than optimised.
automation_rationale: Token and price metering is exact; budget check is arithmetic.
automation_risks: Budget cut-offs abandoning a legally required review mid-way; model price changes invalidating estimates.
validation_evidence_needed: Metered per-run cost on synthetic grants; compare estimate vs actual distribution.
analogy_breaks_down: Cloud unit economics optimises a product margin; here the AI step may be a control, so cost cannot override completion of the control.

capability: Time-driven activity-based costing: capacity cost rate x unit time equations, with unused capacity reported separately
business_problem: Classic ABC via employee time surveys is costly and subjective; costs must follow activities without surveillance.
why_industry_requires: Kaplan & Anderson (HBR 2004) replace surveys with two estimates per pool: cost per unit of practical capacity and time per activity, which also exposes unused capacity.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Economic-model uses FTE = A.g.e.m/(60.H), a TDABC-like formula, but only as a planning model with assumed m; no runtime requirement measures unit times or reports unused capacity.
complexity_challenge: Use time equations with a handful of drivers (exception type, international, rework) per activity, not per-task stopwatch tracking. Unused capacity must not be loaded onto grants, otherwise low December volume looks like high unit cost.
automation_rationale: Unit times are estimated/sampled by humans and refreshed from event timestamps; arithmetic is deterministic.
automation_risks: Event-timestamp durations include waiting; mistaking elapsed time for touch time inflates cost.
validation_evidence_needed: Sample 200 exception cases with touch-time capture; compare with event-derived estimate.
analogy_breaks_down: Manufacturing TDABC assumes stable recipes; DAF exceptions vary widely (EV-106 90 minutes unaided vs 45 assumed), so equations need complexity terms and confidence grades.

capability: Per-transaction activity costing and unit pricing of outsourced back-office work (cost per processed item, per exception, per FTE-hour)
business_problem: Outsourcing contracts price per unit; provider must know unit cost and exception mix to stay profitable.
why_industry_requires: BPO margins depend on handle time, exception rate and utilisation; contracts carry volume bands.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Outsourced-admin and white-label sponsor models (REQ-X-064, REQ-X-071) imply priced service units; REQ-X-071 item 5 names cost-to-serve without definition.
complexity_challenge: Price on outcome units the sponsor understands (settled grant, verified charity, resolved case), not on internal activity steps that change with redesign.
automation_rationale: Unit counts come from authoritative states (settled, verified), not workflow steps.
automation_risks: Pricing on steps rewards keeping steps; pricing on settled grants can pressure unsafe approvals (ADV-577).
validation_evidence_needed: Model at least two pricing units against measured attributed cost.
analogy_breaks_down: BPO provider is not legally responsible for outcomes; a DAF platform operating under sponsor control shares control obligations (SoD floor UNB-ECO-003).

capability: Expense ratio and loss-adjustment expense per claim, split into claim-specific (DCC) and non-claim-specific (A&O) expense
business_problem: Insurers must separate costs directly attributable to a claim from general adjusting overhead for reserving and statutory reporting.
why_industry_requires: Statutory statements and reserving require LAE categories; A&O is everything not attributable to a specific claim.
daf_equivalent_explanation: The DCC/A&O split is the same shape as direct-attributed vs residual cost for a DAF exception case. No DAF requirement separates case-specific cost from pooled case-handling overhead.
complexity_challenge: Adopt only the two-way split (case-specific vs pooled). Do not import reserving or statutory LAE accounting, which has no DAF equivalent.
automation_rationale: Case-specific costs carry a case id; pooled costs go to an activity pool.
automation_risks: Classification drift (as in the 1998 ALAE to DCC reclassification) breaks trend comparisons; version the rule.
validation_evidence_needed: Classify one month of synthetic exception costs; confirm residual share.
analogy_breaks_down: Insurers reserve for future claim cost; DAF exceptions do not create liabilities to reserve (except incidents/recoveries under OD-20).

capability: Claims leakage / cost of poor quality (avoidable cost from errors, rework and over-payment)
business_problem: Money lost to process errors exceeds visible processing cost.
why_industry_requires: Leakage audits quantify avoidable payout and handling cost.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Economic-model §5 proposes an incident cost formula and TVR-ECON-003 requires measuring post-payment review hours; TVF-062 notes correlated failure is absent from cost models. No cost category "cost of failure" on the attribution model.
complexity_challenge: Single cost category "failure and recovery" with sub-types (rework, misdirected payment recovery, post-payment review, service credit). No separate leakage programme.
automation_rationale: Failure costs attach to incident/case ids.
automation_risks: Under-reporting incidents lowers apparent cost (ADV-552 analogue).
validation_evidence_needed: Detection coverage metric alongside failure cost.
analogy_breaks_down: Insurance leakage is mostly overpayment of indemnity; DAF failure cost includes §4966 taxes and reputational harm not reducible to a per-case figure.

capability: Cost per contact and cost per resolution, first-contact resolution, channel cost mix
business_problem: Cost per contact rewards short calls; cost per resolution exposes repeat contacts.
why_industry_requires: Contact centres trade AHT against FCR; channel mix (self-service vs agent) drives cost.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-043 lists support touches and channel transitions (portal/widget/IVR); TVA-019 hypothesises proactive status reduces contacts. No cost-per-resolved-case definition or repeat-contact denominator.
complexity_challenge: Measure cost per resolved donor/charity inquiry (all contacts until resolution) instead of cost per contact; drop AHT as a target.
automation_rationale: Contacts link to a case; resolution is a case state.
automation_risks: Closing cases prematurely to lower cost per resolution; counter-metric reopen rate.
validation_evidence_needed: Synthetic contact log with repeats; compare the two metrics.
analogy_breaks_down: DAF contact volume is low per account and spiky (December); many contacts are status inquiries eliminable by proactive status rather than cheaper handling.

capability: Workforce forecasting and staffing to a service level (Erlang-C or simulation), with intraday/seasonal surge planning
business_problem: Staffing to average volume creates permanent backlogs at peaks.
why_industry_requires: Service level targets require queueing-based staffing, not averages.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Economic-model §3 shows annual-average staffing leaves ~9,600 December cases and ~223 days to clear (TVF-060/TVF-162). Work queues have capacity weighting (REQ-X-048) and a Staffing and Capacity report name (REQ-X-049). No forecasting requirement.
complexity_challenge: Daily-volume queue model with skills pools and SLA clock is enough; Erlang-C assumes Poisson arrivals and no backlog carry-over, which suits contacts but not multi-day review work, so use a simple discrete backlog simulation.
automation_rationale: Forecast is statistical; staffing decisions are human (supervisor/COO).
automation_risks: Forecast built on assumed k = 3 surge multiplier (TVA-004) mistaken for measurement.
validation_evidence_needed: Two prior Decembers of sponsor volume or a shadow replay (EXT-04).
analogy_breaks_down: Contact-centre work is minutes-long and perishable; DAF reviews carry legal competence requirements and cannot be absorbed by generic seasonal agents (TVA-029).

capability: Per-account recordkeeping economics (program-manager basis-point fee plus account maintenance fee; small-account subsidy)
business_problem: Fixed per-account servicing cost against asset-based fees makes small accounts loss-making.
why_industry_requires: Recordkeepers combine bps fees with per-account fees or minimums to cover fixed per-account cost.
daf_equivalent_explanation: DAF fee schedules mirror this: tiered bps with annual minimums ($100 Fidelity, $250 Ren/RCF). Ren/RCF audited payments divided by year-end DAFs are ~$683-$745 but explicitly NOT ARPU.
complexity_challenge: Expose fixed-per-account cost (statements, verification, hosting) separately from activity-driven cost so minimum-fee decisions are evidence-based.
automation_rationale: Arithmetic over attributed costs by balance band.
automation_risks: Using a per-end-year-DAF ratio as ARPU (explicitly warned against in source).
validation_evidence_needed: Attributed fixed cost per account-month from one sponsor.
analogy_breaks_down: 529 accounts are owned by the participant; DAF funds are sponsor property, and minimum fees reduce charitable assets, which raises reasonableness questions a 529 plan does not have.

capability: Process mining over the event log (variants, rework loops, wait vs touch time, touch count, conformance)
business_problem: Inefficient paths are invisible in aggregate KPIs.
why_industry_requires: Event-log mining reconstructs actual process variants and quantifies rework and waiting.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-042 learns from exception signals; Echelon continuous-improvement method lists redundant activities and excessive processing time as signals; WQ Performance view lists rework and time by stage. No requirement to mine the full event log including happy paths.
complexity_challenge: Mine the existing outbox/domain events (REQ-X-043) rather than adding instrumentation; start with five measures: variant count, rework rate, wait share, touches per outcome, handoffs per case.
automation_rationale: Variant discovery and timing are algorithmic; interpretation is human/AI-assisted.
automation_risks: Mistaking legally required second review for "rework"; must tag control steps as non-eliminable.
validation_evidence_needed: Mine a synthetic replay with seeded rework loops and verify detection.
analogy_breaks_down: Manufacturing process mining assumes all steps are optimisable; DAF processes contain statutory/fiduciary steps (PRINCIPLES classification) which are constraints, not waste.

capability: Cost of poor quality (COPQ) with control counter-metrics; improvement targets with guardrails
business_problem: Cost programmes cut controls and quality silently.
why_industry_requires: Balanced scorecards pair efficiency with quality/risk metrics.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-042 requires guardrails and regressions; REQ-X-043 warns "Avoid optimizing processing speed at the expense of compliance or donor trust". No configured floors that block a cost target ratchet.
complexity_challenge: One small fixed set of counter-metrics with numeric floors, configured per sponsor, instead of a composite health score (which REQ-X-043 rejects).
automation_rationale: Floor breach is a threshold comparison.
automation_risks: Floors set too low to be meaningful; floors not measured (detection coverage).
validation_evidence_needed: Inject a cost-saving change that degrades false-negative rate in replay; confirm ratchet blocked.
analogy_breaks_down: Manufacturing defects are observable; DAF control failures (missed sanctions, taxable distributions) are rare and often detected late, so floors need leading indicators.

capability: Automation ROI measured on realised net savings including oversight, rework, exceptions and run cost
business_problem: Automation business cases overstate savings by ignoring exception handling and maintenance.
why_industry_requires: Programmes must re-measure realised benefits after deployment.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Echelon economics engine computes design-time savings with verdicts and sensitivity; ADV-566 warns labour savings omit rework. No runtime ROI verification.
complexity_challenge: Use the same Echelon cost model fields at runtime with measured values replacing estimates (Observation source) instead of a separate ROI tool.
automation_rationale: Comparison of measured attributed costs pre/post with confidence grades.
automation_risks: Seasonality and mix shifts masquerade as savings; need matched periods or cohorts.
validation_evidence_needed: Pre/post comparison on replay with seeded mix change.
analogy_breaks_down: RPA replaces keystrokes; AI-native redesign removes steps, so the baseline may not exist post-change; requires a frozen baseline.

capability: Step-down / reciprocal allocation of support-department costs and reconciliation of allocations to GL
business_problem: Allocated totals drift from the books and lose credibility.
why_industry_requires: Management accounts must tie to the GL; unallocated amounts are shown, not hidden.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-ACC-014 mentions "allocation methodologies" inside the accounting system without stating whether management allocations post, or how they reconcile. No residual concept.
complexity_challenge: Single-step direct allocation plus explicit residual is enough; reciprocal methods add complexity without decision value at DAF scale.
automation_risks: Silent spreading of residual through a "plug" driver.
validation_evidence_needed: Monthly reconciliation run on mock GL.
analogy_breaks_down: DAF sponsors also prepare statutory functional-expense allocations (Form 990 Part IX); management ABC and statutory functional allocation must be distinct and both traceable to GL.

capability: Functional expense allocation (program / management and general / fundraising) for statutory reporting
business_problem: Charities must report expenses by function; allocation choices are audited.
why_industry_requires: Form 990 Part IX and nonprofit GAAP require functional expense presentation.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-ACC-019 requires functional expenses "where required". daf-landscape used Part IX to compute sponsor operating cost per grant ($55-$68 at largest nationals; $134 Vanguard; $419 NPT).
complexity_challenge: Let the cost attribution model supply evidence to (not replace) the CPA-approved functional allocation; one source of activity data, two governed views.
automation_rationale: Functional allocation policy is a CPA/auditor judgement.
automation_risks: Management ABC figures re-used as statutory without review.
validation_evidence_needed: CPA review of mapping from activities to functions.
analogy_breaks_down: This is DAF-native (statutory), not an analogy; the risk is conflating it with management costing.

capability: Payment rail cost comparison and least-cost routing subject to constraints (ACH vs check vs wire vs card)
business_problem: Rail choice drives per-payment cost by an order of magnitude.
why_industry_requires: Banks route to cheapest compliant rail.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Payment requirements define rails, proof and Unknown handling (REQ-X-083); no requirement quotes cost per rail before selection or reports check-handling cost (ADV-565 notes unit cost can exclude paper/check overhead).
complexity_challenge: Do not auto-route on cost; recipient payment method is a verified recipient fact. Use cost quotes to drive recipient enrollment campaigns (ACH onboarding) via REQ-X-042.
automation_rationale: Rail fee schedules are contract data.
automation_risks: Cost-driven rail switching that sends funds to an unverified account.
validation_evidence_needed: Rail fee schedule ingestion for three rails in mock mode.
analogy_breaks_down: Banks own the customer instruction; DAF recipient method must match verified bank ownership, so cost is a secondary criterion.

capability: Pre-commitment cost quote for international grants (equivalency determination / expenditure responsibility, FX, wire charges)
business_problem: International grants carry large fixed review cost that can exceed the grant value.
why_industry_requires: Grantmakers disclose ED/ER fees or minimum grant sizes because review cost is material.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-GRANT-041, UNB-WF-006 and REQ-X-065 cover controls; FI-36 assigns charge bearer for foreign wire fees. No cost quote or minimum-economic-size rule.
complexity_challenge: Quote and disclose; do not silently decline small international grants on cost. Fee policy remains sponsor-authorised.
automation_rationale: Quote = configured fee schedule + metered/estimated third-party ED cost + FX spread.
automation_risks: Quote presented as binding when third-party ED cost is uncertain.
validation_evidence_needed: Synthetic quotes vs final attributed cost on mock ED cases.
analogy_breaks_down: Commercial cross-border payments are priced for profit; DAF ED review is a legal control whose cost may be borne by the fund only under sponsor policy.

capability: Customer lifetime value, gross/net revenue retention and cohort economics
business_problem: Acquisition and service spend must be justified by lifetime margin.
why_industry_requires: Subscription businesses manage to LTV/CAC and NRR.
daf_equivalent_explanation: daf-landscape revenue-cohort sensitivity models GRR/NRR (hypothetical, no observed revenue). Institutional sponsor economics (Model C/D, UNB-COM-001) resemble SaaS contracts.
complexity_challenge: Apply LTV at sponsor/partner-contract level only. Donor-level LTV is a marketing concept and must not feed any compliance, approval or servicing priority.
automation_risks: Donor LTV scores leaking into routing or grant review priority.
validation_evidence_needed: Two years of contract revenue for any partner.
analogy_breaks_down: DAF revenue is mostly asset-based and moves with markets and granting, not churn; NRR conflates market moves with retention (source warns).

capability: Simulation of alternative service and pricing strategies (tiers, minimums, per-transaction fees, pass-through)
business_problem: Price changes have revenue, cost, adoption and fairness consequences that are hard to foresee.
why_industry_requires: Price/volume/cost simulation before change.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-ENT-003 requires sensitivity-tested unit economics; Echelon Economics engine runs expected/sensitivity/corner/scale scenarios with verdicts; daf-landscape fee scenarios illustrate tier outcomes. No runtime scenario engine grounded in measured drivers.
