complexity_challenge: Reuse the Echelon three-point/corner/verdict method on measured drivers; do not build an optimiser.
automation_risks: Scenario outputs mistaken for forecasts; illustrative inputs presented as facts.
validation_evidence_needed: Back-test one scenario against a later observed month.
analogy_breaks_down: Commercial pricing optimises profit; DAF fees reduce charitable assets and must be reasonable and disclosed; simulation informs, sponsor board decides.

capability: Fee recovery and cost-recovery ratio for configurable service charges (special requests)
business_problem: Special services consume disproportionate cost; flat fees cross-subsidise.
why_industry_requires: Regulated and public-sector fee setting documents cost-recovery basis.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-ACC-010 supports fee schedules, waivers, allocations; Fidelity excludes "special requests" from admin fee (daf-economics-sources E06). No link from service charge to attributed cost or recovery ratio.
complexity_challenge: Report recovery ratio (charge revenue / attributed cost) per configured charge; leave the fee decision to the sponsor.
automation_risks: Charges set above cost against charitable assets may raise reasonableness or private-benefit questions; counsel review.
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel review of permitted service charges to funds.
analogy_breaks_down: Public fees recover cost from beneficiaries; DAF charges reduce assets already irrevocably given to charity.

capability: Service-level economics: cost of meeting each SLA tier, service credits, cost-of-delay
business_problem: SLA tiers are sold without knowing the incremental cost of tighter targets.
why_industry_requires: Outsourcers price SLA tiers on staffing and redundancy cost.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-071 requires tiered SLAs and service-credit implications; no requirement computes the staffing cost of each SLA tier.
complexity_challenge: Derive SLA-tier cost from the capacity model (staff needed to hit p90 at December peak) instead of separate pricing tools.
automation_risks: Selling an SLA tier the specialist pool cannot meet in December.
validation_evidence_needed: Capacity model run for two SLA tiers at k = 2 and 3.
analogy_breaks_down: IT SLAs are about availability; DAF SLAs are about legally gated decisions that cannot be accelerated by redundancy alone.

capability: Tenant-level cost attribution for shared infrastructure and noisy-neighbour cost
business_problem: Shared platforms cannot price or detect tenants that consume disproportionate resources.
why_industry_requires: SaaS cost-per-tenant drives pricing and isolation-tier decisions.
daf_equivalent_explanation: ADR-009 lists isolation tier economics at 10/100/1,000 tenants; UNB-TEN-015 requires noisy-neighbour detection; UNB-RCN-PLT-012 requires cost in TenantIsolationDecision. No cost attribution per tenant.
complexity_challenge: Attribute by event counts and storage bytes per sponsor (grade C), not by per-query metering.
automation_risks: Cost data revealing a sponsor’s volumes to another sponsor.
analogy_breaks_down: SaaS tenants are customers; here dedicated-isolation decisions are also regulatory/contractual (UNB-RCN-PLT-012), not only cost.

capability: Cost per verification and reuse economics of shared determinations
business_problem: Re-verifying the same charity per sponsor multiplies vendor and review cost.
why_industry_requires: KYB providers price per check; reuse lowers marginal cost.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-KNOW-029 tracks acquisition/compute/storage/review cost per source; REQ-X-042 notes reuse of platform-wide verified evidence; TVA-020 questions legal reliance on shared determinations.
complexity_challenge: Attribute shared verification cost to sponsors by reuse count; never let lower cost justify reliance that counsel has not approved.
automation_risks: Cost savings from reuse claimed before counsel confirms reliance (TVA-020).
validation_evidence_needed: Counsel decision on reuse; mock reuse counts.
analogy_breaks_down: KYB vendors carry no legal duty; sponsor retains §4966 responsibility for each grant.

capability: Attribution of custody, investment-management and banking fees (bps, per-transaction, analysis charges) to funds/pools and to sponsor operations
business_problem: Some costs are borne by funds (inside NAV) and others by the sponsor; mixing them mis-states operating cost.
why_industry_requires: Asset managers separate fund expenses from manager operating expense.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-INV-025 and UNB-ACC-009 define investment fee posting; daf-landscape notes investment fees netted inside funds are invisible in Part IX. No rule distinguishes fund-borne from sponsor-borne cost in cost-to-serve views.
complexity_challenge: Tag every cost line with "bearer" (fund, sponsor, platform, partner) and exclude fund-borne costs from operating cost-to-serve, showing them separately as donor all-in cost.
automation_risks: Double counting fund-borne fees as sponsor cost or omitting them from donor all-in cost.
validation_evidence_needed: Mock custodian statement with bps and per-trade fees.
analogy_breaks_down: Bank fee analysis statements charge the account holder; here the account holder may be the sponsor on behalf of pooled funds.

capability: Configurable cost and margin thresholds with alerting and owners
business_problem: Overruns are noticed at quarter end.
why_industry_requires: Budget variance alerts with named owners.
daf_equivalent_explanation: UNB-ACC-014 budgets and actual-vs-budget; CTL-027 AI cost anomalies. No configurable unit-cost/margin thresholds on attributed cost.
complexity_challenge: Thresholds only on grade A/B metrics by default; C/D metrics alert on trend not level.
automation_risks: Alert fatigue; thresholds that trigger automatic service reductions.
analogy_breaks_down: Corporate budgets are discretionary; some DAF costs are non-discretionary controls.

capability: Continuous cost-reduction loop with ratcheting targets (kaizen / productivity ratchet)
business_problem: Cost programmes are episodic and regress.
why_industry_requires: Lean organisations institutionalise measured improvement with standard work updates.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-042 has a continuous improvement workflow; Echelon continuous-improvement method defines Observe..Verify; neither has cost targets, ratchet rule, counter-metric floors or owners.
complexity_challenge: Extend REQ-X-042 workflow with cost targets rather than creating a separate programme.
automation_rationale: Detection and verification deterministic; hypotheses AI-assisted; approval human.
automation_risks: Goodhart effects; ratchet below structural SoD floor (UNB-ECO-003).
validation_evidence_needed: Two quarter replay with seeded improvement and seeded regression.
analogy_breaks_down: Manufacturing kaizen improves repeatable tasks; DAF floors (SoD, legally competent review) bound achievable reduction.

capability: Forecasting spend and pre-deployment cost estimates (cost guardrails before expensive operations)
business_problem: Expensive operations are launched without knowing cost.
why_industry_requires: FinOps forecasting and policy-as-code budget checks.
daf_equivalent_explanation: AIN-028 budgets; no pre-check quote; no forecast of AI or vendor spend for December.
complexity_challenge: Only operations above a configured estimated-cost threshold get a pre-check; everything else is metered after the fact.
automation_rationale: Estimate from rate card x expected units.
analogy_breaks_down: Cloud estimates are for engineers; DAF quotes may be donor-facing, requiring disclosure accuracy.

capability: AI-generated improvement recommendations with evidence (advisory only)
business_problem: Analysts cannot inspect every variant and cost driver.
why_industry_requires: AI can summarise mined variants and propose hypotheses.
daf_equivalent_explanation: REQ-X-042 allows AI to investigate and propose but not self-modify; REQ-X-055 proactive assistance. No requirement for cost-specific recommendation content (expected saving range, counter-metric risk, evidence).
complexity_challenge: Recommendations enter REQ-X-042 InterventionProposal; no new path.
automation_rationale: Pattern explanation benefits from language models; decisions do not.
validation_evidence_needed: Seeded replay with known causes; precision of recommendations.
analogy_breaks_down: Commercial ops AI may auto-tune; here policy changes require sponsor/human authority.

capability: Cost of human approvals and four-eyes controls as an explicit control cost (cost per approval, approvals per outcome)
business_problem: Controls accumulate; their cost is never weighed against risk reduced.
why_industry_requires: Control rationalisation programmes measure cost per control execution.
daf_equivalent_explanation: Decision rights (REQ-X-044) and SoD (UNB-ACC-022) define approvals; no measurement of cost per approval or approvals per settled grant.
complexity_challenge: Measure, never auto-remove: approval cost is an input to Tier C governance review, which alone can change a control.
automation_rationale: Approvals are recorded events with durations.
automation_risks: Cost pressure to remove legally required approvals.
analogy_breaks_down: Bank control rationalisation may drop redundant checks freely; statutory/fiduciary DAF controls cannot be dropped on cost.

capability: Cost per manual exception by exception type and root cause
business_problem: Exception handling is the dominant variable labour cost.
why_industry_requires: Exception cost by type drives automation priority.
daf_equivalent_explanation: FX doc lists human touches, AI touches per exception; economic-model per-account exception cost; no cost per exception type attributed from measured time.
complexity_challenge: Rank root causes by attributed cost x recurrence, feed REQ-X-042.
automation_rationale: Time equation x capacity cost rate.
automation_risks: Cheap-to-handle but high-harm exceptions deprioritised; rank by harm-weighted cost.
validation_evidence_needed: Exception type taxonomy coverage on replay.
analogy_breaks_down: BPO exceptions are client-defined; DAF exceptions include legal referrals with asymmetric harm.

capability: External cost benchmarks (Form 990 operating cost per grant / per account / bps) as calibration ranges
business_problem: Internal costs lack external reference.
why_industry_requires: Benchmarks calibrate plausibility.
daf_equivalent_explanation: daf-landscape computed FY2024 DAF-allocated operating cost 67 bps (assets basis) / 89 bps (grants basis); nationals $55-$68 per grant at largest scale; IT median 2.8% of operating cost.
complexity_challenge: Use as sanity ranges only, labelled sourced-benchmark per UNB-ECO-002.
automation_risks: Benchmarks treated as targets; scope mismatch (affiliate costs invisible in Part IX).
analogy_breaks_down: Part IX shows function not process; costs borne by affiliates are hidden (BofA $0.1m on $4.73bn).

capability: Commitment/discount and vendor rate-card management (effective vs billed cost)
business_problem: List-price attribution overstates cost; discounts unallocated.
why_industry_requires: FOCUS separates ListCost, ContractedCost, BilledCost, EffectiveCost.
daf_equivalent_explanation: No requirement distinguishes list from effective cost for vendors (model API commitments, payment volume tiers).
complexity_challenge: Attribute at effective cost; keep list cost for scenario comparison only.
automation_risks: Tier discounts that apply retroactively change prior attributed costs; handle as restatement with version.
analogy_breaks_down: Some DAF vendors price on AUM bps, which FOCUS does not model natively.

capability: Posting journal as system of record (journal = financial event log)
business_problem: Balances must be provable from one immutable record
why_industry_requires: Regulated deposit balances are derived from postings
daf_equivalent_explanation: DAF fund balances are sponsor-entity journal postings with fund dimension
complexity_challenge: Simplify: do not add an event store beneath the journal
analogy_breaks_down: Bank deposits are liabilities to customers; DAF funds are sponsor-owned net assets with advisory privileges

capability: Available-balance hold/authorization reservation checked synchronously
business_problem: Prevent overspend under concurrency
why_industry_requires: Card authorizations must not exceed available funds
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant reservation against fund capacity
complexity_challenge: Keep single-transaction reservation; no async capacity events
automation_risks: Lock contention at year-end on popular funds (rare)
analogy_breaks_down: Card holds expire automatically; grant reservations persist until disposition

capability: Return processing keyed by network trace and return reason
business_problem: Returns arrive days later without end-to-end keys
why_industry_requires: Nacha return windows
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant and contribution ACH returns (R03 etc.)
complexity_challenge: Key derivation registry rather than per-adapter ad hoc logic
analogy_breaks_down: Unbound is not the ODFI; depends on partner bank file formats

capability: Payee bank change controls and pinned destination at release
business_problem: Account takeover reroutes payments
why_industry_requires: BEC fraud
daf_equivalent_explanation: Charity bank change vs in-flight grant payment
complexity_challenge: Already well specified
analogy_breaks_down: Charities change banks rarely; cooling-off acceptable

capability: Trade lifecycle with partial fills and busts
business_problem: Proceeds arrive in pieces and can be corrected
why_industry_requires: Exchange/custodian behaviour
daf_equivalent_explanation: In-kind liquidation tranches; redemption legs
complexity_challenge: Process manager per liquidation; no saga engine
analogy_breaks_down: DAF rarely trades actively; mostly liquidation and pooled funds

capability: Expected-file calendar, control totals and late-data handling
business_problem: Silent missing data
why_industry_requires: Daily custody reconciliations
daf_equivalent_explanation: Custodian/bank/IRS feeds
complexity_challenge: Simple calendar + watermark
analogy_breaks_down: Market data uses sequence numbers; DAF feeds are files without sequences

capability: Sequence-gap detection and recovery
business_problem: Detect lost messages
why_industry_requires: Order books need complete sequences
daf_equivalent_explanation: Only for providers exposing sequences; DB sequences must not be used for gap inference
complexity_challenge: Do not import gap-fill protocols; use claim-and-mark outbox
automation_risks: False gap alarms from DB sequence holes
analogy_breaks_down: DAF event rates are tiny; PostgreSQL sequences are not gapless

capability: Period close, locks and prior-period adjustments
business_problem: Issued statements must not change
why_industry_requires: Audit and statutory reporting
daf_equivalent_explanation: Monthly fund statements, annual 990/Schedule D
complexity_challenge: Lock rule is one row lock
analogy_breaks_down: DAF needs fund-level statements to donors, which ERP closes do not issue

capability: Reports from sealed as-of datasets
business_problem: Reproducibility
why_industry_requires: Supervisory reporting
daf_equivalent_explanation: Statements, Schedule D package, audit
complexity_challenge: Watermark filter, no separate warehouse
analogy_breaks_down: DAF volumes allow computing from the live DB at a watermark

capability: Transactional outbox and idempotent consumers
business_problem: Avoid dual writes
why_industry_requires: Orders + messages
daf_equivalent_explanation: Payments dispatch, notices, partner webhooks
complexity_challenge: Keep; avoid broker
analogy_breaks_down: Payments are irreversible; e-commerce can refund

capability: Saga with compensations
business_problem: Multi-step business transactions
why_industry_requires: Inventory/payment/shipping
daf_equivalent_explanation: Compensation exists (returns, reversals) but cannot undo external payments
complexity_challenge: Use single transaction for internal steps; compensations only for external effects
analogy_breaks_down: External payment finality breaks symmetric compensation

capability: One claim number correlating reserves, payments, recoveries, correspondence
business_problem: Complete claim file
why_industry_requires: Claims audit
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant/contribution correlation root across capabilities
complexity_challenge: Correlation root + parent root
analogy_breaks_down: Claims reserves are estimates; DAF reservations are exact

capability: Exception repair queues for stuck straight-through processing
business_problem: Humans fix only what rules cannot
why_industry_requires: STP repair
daf_equivalent_explanation: Human-resolution queue for stalled process managers and poison events
complexity_challenge: One queue model, typed resolutions
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Mutable relationship data with field history
business_problem: Engagement management
why_industry_requires: Sales/service
daf_equivalent_explanation: Engagement data only; authority facts separate
complexity_challenge: Do not event-source CRM
analogy_breaks_down: Donors do not own the assets; advisory privilege is a legal relationship with the sponsor

capability: Joint account instruction authority (any/all)
business_problem: Conflicting owner instructions
why_industry_requires: Joint accounts
daf_equivalent_explanation: Multi-advisor funds
complexity_challenge: Policy per instruction kind
analogy_breaks_down: Sponsor, not advisors, decides; advisors only recommend

capability: Real-time screening and blocking at release and transmission
business_problem: Strict liability
why_industry_requires: OFAC
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant payments, contributions
complexity_challenge: Per-item check; no batch authority
automation_rationale: List matching rules; humans for true-match
analogy_breaks_down: DAF also screens donors and advisors, not only payees

capability: Typed holds: asset freeze vs legal records hold vs sanctions block
business_problem: Precise blocking
why_industry_requires: Litigation and garnishment
daf_equivalent_explanation: Fund disputes, records holds, sanctions
complexity_challenge: Typed holds with command matrix
analogy_breaks_down: Charitable distributions are the purpose; over-freezing harms charities

capability: Re-rating usage after correction
business_problem: Fees on corrected bases
why_industry_requires: Billing disputes
daf_equivalent_explanation: Fee accrual recompute after AUM/NAV correction
complexity_challenge: Delta postings, not re-billing
analogy_breaks_down: Fee is charged to charitable assets; disclosure rules apply

capability: NAV error correction with materiality policy
business_problem: Correct unit holders after pricing errors
why_industry_requires: Investor protection
daf_equivalent_explanation: Pooled DAF investment NAV restatement
complexity_challenge: Materiality threshold avoids reprocessing trivia
analogy_breaks_down: DAF fund holders are not investors with redemption rights

capability: Full event sourcing of ledger and domain
business_problem: Audit and replay
why_industry_requires: Startups' design choice
daf_equivalent_explanation: Journal already append-only; ES adds a second log
complexity_challenge: Reject full ES; keep append-only facts with in-tx state
analogy_breaks_down: ES is a design choice, not an industry requirement

capability: Tenant migration with watermark and writer fencing
business_problem: Move tenants without loss
why_industry_requires: Isolation tiers
daf_equivalent_explanation: Sponsor moves between isolation profiles
complexity_challenge: Fewer profiles (RCD-004)
analogy_breaks_down: Tenant = legal sponsor; moving between sponsors is not migration

capability: Account portfolio conversion between legal entities
business_problem: Transfer books between institutions
why_industry_requires: Acquisitions
daf_equivalent_explanation: Bulk sponsor-to-sponsor fund transfer
complexity_challenge: Per-fund legal transfer with program PM
analogy_breaks_down: Each DAF transfer is a charitable distribution subject to sponsor discretion

capability: Send-time revalidation of alerts
business_problem: False alerts
why_industry_requires: Customer trust
daf_equivalent_explanation: Grant paid/returned notices
complexity_challenge: Single read before send
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Model outputs as inputs, never bookings
business_problem: AI cannot create records of account
why_industry_requires: Model risk
daf_equivalent_explanation: AI observations vs facts
complexity_challenge: Types + DB roles
analogy_breaks_down: DAF law reserves discretion to sponsor (IRC 4966(d)(2)) — stronger than banking guidance

capability: Published integration events separate from internal events
business_problem: Stable partner contracts
why_industry_requires: Partner ecosystems
daf_equivalent_explanation: Widget/checkout/partner webhooks
complexity_challenge: Small published surface
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Quantified gate for brokers/services
business_problem: Avoid premature distribution
why_industry_requires: Cost control
daf_equivalent_explanation: Single PostgreSQL per sponsor with outbox
complexity_challenge: Explicit thresholds
analogy_breaks_down: n/a

capability: Change-data-capture to analytics
business_problem: Analytics without OLTP load
why_industry_requires: BI
daf_equivalent_explanation: Optional analytics feed only
complexity_challenge: Defer; snapshots suffice
analogy_breaks_down: Not needed for authoritative reporting
